holdings_preview.ticker_note: Operates a pan-South American airline network with domestic businesses in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Peru and Ecuador. Its widebody international routes connect Latin America with North America, Europe and Oceania, while LATAM Cargo adds dedicated regional and international airfreight operations.

Uses Panama City's Tocumen Airport as a connecting hub linking North, Central and South America. Its Boeing 737 fleet connects markets that may not support nonstop international flights, while Wingo provides a separate low-cost airline operation serving price-sensitive regional travelers.

Operates a broad Brazilian domestic network connecting major cities and smaller communities using Airbus and Embraer aircraft. Its geographic reach into underserved Brazilian markets and reliance on domestic connecting traffic differentiate its operations from airlines concentrated on international trunk routes.

Operates Mexico's principal full-service network airline, connecting Mexico City with domestic, U.S., European and Asian destinations. Its Delta commercial relationship, SkyTeam participation, Aeromexico Rewards program and premium corporate-travel position distinguish it from Mexico's ultra-low-cost carriers.

Operates Volaris, an ultra-low-cost airline connecting Mexico, the United States and Central America. Its high-density Airbus fleet, separately priced baggage and seat selection, and visiting-friends-and-relatives traffic create distinct exposure to price-sensitive Mexican and cross-border passenger demand.

Operates extensive Caribbean and Latin American services from Fort Lauderdale, Orlando, New York and San Juan. Its October 2026 Barranquilla launch, expanded Cartagena service and additional Dominican Republic frequencies reinforce its role in connecting U.S. travelers with Latin American destinations.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Domino's relies on pizza orders, delivery occasions and add-on purchases including sides, desserts and drinks. PwC identified pizza as the restaurant category with the largest GLP-1 household spending decline, creating potential pressure on order frequency, basket size and franchisee sales.

Papa John's sells delivery and carryout pizzas alongside breadsticks, chicken sides, desserts and beverages. Its pizza-centered menu offers limited natural portion flexibility, while reduced group orders or fewer add-on purchases could weaken transaction values and royalty-generating restaurant sales.

The Cheesecake Factory is known for large entree portions, extensive menus and signature cheesecakes. Customers seeking smaller meals or skipping desserts could reduce average checks, while substantial restaurant labor and occupancy costs make company-operated locations sensitive to revenue declines.

BJ's operates casual dining restaurants featuring deep-dish pizza, burgers, shareable appetizers and Pizookie desserts. Its combination of indulgent meals, alcohol and discretionary dessert purchases exposes multiple check-building categories to appetite suppression and changing restaurant-ordering habits.

Texas Roadhouse operates steak-focused restaurants with substantial entrees, complimentary bread, appetizers and alcoholic beverages. GLP-1 users may continue purchasing protein-rich steaks but reduce sides, starters and drinks, potentially compressing average checks without materially reducing kitchen or labor requirements.

Brinker operates Chili's and Maggiano's, offering burgers, ribs, pasta, appetizers and alcoholic beverages. Chili's Triple Dipper and bundled meal promotions encourage multi-item orders, while Maggiano's family-style Italian dining creates additional exposure to reduced portion demand and fewer discretionary additions.

Bloomin' operates Outback Steakhouse, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill and Fleming's. Its concepts combine large entrees, shareable appetizers and beverage sales, leaving check averages potentially vulnerable if GLP-1 users reduce starters, desserts or alcoholic drinks while retaining main courses.

Darden operates Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse, Cheddar's and several upscale dining brands. Olive Garden's unlimited soup, salad and breadsticks proposition and pasta-heavy menu face potential portion compression, although the company's steak concepts and diversified restaurant portfolio moderate overall exposure.

Wingstop specializes in chicken wings, tenders, fries and flavored beverages, frequently sold in multi-piece orders and group bundles. Reduced appetite could encourage smaller wing quantities and fewer fries or drinks, although protein-oriented menu items may remain attractive to GLP-1 users.

Dine Brands franchises Applebee's and IHOP, combining casual dining with pancake-focused breakfast occasions. Applebee's appetizers and desserts and IHOP's pancakes, syrups and bundled breakfasts face potential order-mix pressure, primarily affecting franchise royalty revenue through lower systemwide sales.

Red Robin operates burger-focused casual dining restaurants offering large burgers, bottomless fries, shakes and alcoholic beverages. Its oversized meals and indulgent extras create potential exposure to customers ordering less, while company-operated restaurant economics amplify the effect of lower check averages.

Cracker Barrel serves traditional comfort-food breakfasts, country dinners and homestyle sides through company-operated restaurants. Its large plated meals and biscuit-heavy breakfast offerings could face reduced consumption, although the attached retail stores provide a separate revenue stream unrelated to portion sizes.

Jack in the Box emphasizes burgers, tacos, late-night meals, combo orders and indulgent sides. Reduced spontaneous eating and smaller meal bundles could pressure franchise sales, particularly in late-night occasions, although value promotions and an expanding franchised model dilute direct exposure.

Portillo's specializes in Chicago-style hot dogs, Italian beef sandwiches, burgers, cheese fries and chocolate cake shakes. Its indulgent menu and combination-meal occasions face potential pressure from reduced appetite, while company-operated restaurants remain exposed to labor and occupancy costs if average checks decline.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Brown-Forman concentrates on distilled spirits led by Jack Daniel's Tennessee Whiskey, Woodford Reserve and Herradura tequila. Fiscal 2026 U.S. sales were pressured partly by lower Jack Daniel's volumes, making further reductions in drinking occasions a potential headwind to its core whiskey franchise.

Diageo owns Johnnie Walker, Smirnoff, Captain Morgan, Don Julio and Guinness, spanning spirits and beer. Its broad exposure to drinking occasions creates potential volume pressure if GLP-1 users reduce alcohol intake, although Guinness 0.0 and other nonalcoholic offerings provide partial substitution opportunities.

Pernod Ricard owns Absolut vodka, Jameson whiskey, Chivas Regal, Ballantine's and Martell cognac. Fiscal 2026 results showed weakness in several major international spirits brands, particularly in the United States and China, leaving its spirits-focused portfolio sensitive to further drinking-frequency reductions.

Campari owns Aperol, Campari, Espolòn tequila, Wild Turkey bourbon and Grand Marnier. Its brands depend on cocktail occasions, aperitifs and spirits consumption in bars and homes, making reduced alcohol cravings potentially relevant to both bottle volumes and cocktail-related demand.

Treasury Wine Estates owns Penfolds, DAOU, 19 Crimes, Beringer and Matua. Its premium and commercial wine operations depend on repeated drinking occasions and restaurant or home consumption, while weaker U.S. wine demand and inventory adjustments have already complicated operating performance.

Constellation's beer business generated approximately $8.3 billion in fiscal 2026 sales, led by Modelo, Corona and Pacifico in the United States. Reduced alcohol consumption could pressure beer depletions and brewery utilization, although Corona Non-Alcoholic and other extensions offer potential offsets.

AB InBev owns Budweiser, Bud Light, Stella Artois, Michelob Ultra and numerous regional beer brands. Its enormous global brewing network depends on recurring beer consumption, while Michelob Ultra Zero and Corona Cero provide nonalcoholic alternatives that could capture some substitution spending.

Heineken sells Heineken, Amstel, Birra Moretti and other beer brands through global brewing and distribution operations. Reduced drinking frequency could affect beer volumes and capacity utilization, although Heineken 0.0 gives the company a well-established nonalcoholic alternative within its flagship franchise.

Boston Beer produces Samuel Adams beer, Twisted Tea, Truly Hard Seltzer and Dogfish Head beverages. Its flavored malt and hard-seltzer businesses rely on discretionary social drinking, while Truly and Twisted Tea compete for occasions that GLP-1 users may increasingly skip.

Molson Coors owns Coors Light, Miller Lite, Blue Moon and other beer brands concentrated in North American and European markets. Fewer drinking occasions could reduce mainstream beer volumes, although its portfolio expansion into nonalcoholic and alternative beverages partially moderates the risk.

Ambev brews Brahma, Skol, Antarctica and other beers across Latin America while also distributing soft drinks. Reduced drinking occasions could pressure beer volumes in Brazil and regional markets, although developing-market GLP-1 penetration and its nonalcoholic beverage operations temper immediate exposure.

Carlsberg owns Carlsberg, Tuborg, 1664 and regional brewing brands across Europe and Asia. Its breweries face potential alcoholic-beverage volume pressure from reduced drinking frequency, while alcohol-free beer and its expanded soft-drink portfolio provide important alternative revenue channels.

Becle owns José Cuervo, 1800 Tequila, Maestro Dobel and additional spirits brands, with significant tequila exposure. Reduced demand for shots, margaritas and at-home spirits consumption could affect its product volumes, although premium tequila pricing and geographic diversification may offset some declines.

Rémy Cointreau produces Rémy Martin cognac, Cointreau orange liqueur and premium spirits. Its concentrated portfolio depends on discretionary spirits consumption and cocktail occasions; reduced drinking could compound existing demand challenges, although gifting, premiumization and international market differences complicate direct GLP-1 attribution.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Lilly commercializes Zepbound and Mounjaro through tirzepatide, a dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist. Its portfolio also includes oral GLP-1 drug orforglipron and Phase 3 triple agonist retatrutide, providing exposure to established obesity sales and potentially differentiated next-generation treatment mechanisms.

Novo commercializes semaglutide through Wegovy and Ozempic, including oral Wegovy in the United States. Its pipeline includes CagriSema, cagrilintide and zenagamtide, combining GLP-1 and amylin pathways to pursue better efficacy, tolerability and formulation choices.

Amgen's MariTide combines GLP-1 receptor activation with GIP receptor antagonism using an antibody-peptide conjugate. Its Phase 3 obesity program tests a differentiated approach with potential for less frequent administration than conventional weekly injectable incretin therapies.

Viking develops VK2735, a dual GLP-1/GIP agonist with injectable and oral formulations. Its Phase 3 injectable development and oral clinical program create concentrated exposure to weight-loss efficacy, dosing flexibility and the commercialization potential of an independent obesity-drug franchise.

Structure develops aleniglipron, an oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist designed to provide substantial weight loss without injections. Its oral drug-development focus differentiates it from peptide injection specialists, with clinical efficacy, gastrointestinal tolerability and dosing convenience central to its competitive position.

Zealand is advancing petrelintide, a long-acting amylin analog, through a major collaboration with Roche. The companies are also developing combinations with Roche's CT-388, targeting appetite regulation through complementary pathways rather than relying exclusively on conventional GLP-1 agonism.

Innovent commercializes mazdutide in China following regulatory approval for chronic weight management. The dual glucagon/GLP-1 receptor agonist offers a differentiated metabolic mechanism, making Innovent one of the few publicly traded Chinese biotechnology companies with an approved obesity-specific incretin treatment.

Kailera develops ribupatide, a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist in injectable and oral formulations, alongside oral candidate KAI-7535 and triple agonist KAI-4729. Its obesity-focused clinical pipeline offers several dosing and receptor-mechanism approaches within a single emerging pharmaceutical developer.

Roche is developing CT-388, an injectable GLP-1/GIP dual agonist, and is collaborating with Zealand Pharma on petrelintide and combination therapies. Its obesity strategy combines an internal incretin asset with an externally partnered amylin platform and global clinical-development capabilities.

United Laboratories originated UBT251, a GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist licensed to Novo Nordisk outside Greater China. Its subsidiary retains regional rights, while the licensing agreement provides potential milestone and royalty economics tied to development and commercialization.

Pfizer acquired Metsera in November 2025, adding injectable GLP-1 candidate MET-097i, amylin analog MET-233i and an oral GLP-1 development program. Its portfolio provides exposure to longer-acting injections and combination obesity therapies beyond its existing pharmaceutical businesses.

Altimmune develops pemvidutide, a balanced GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist focused primarily on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis. Its Phase 3 MASH development connects weight reduction with liver-fat and metabolic outcomes, differentiating it from obesity developers targeting weight loss alone.

Hengrui developed HRS-1596, an investigational once-weekly oral GLP-1/GIP dual agonist. Its September 2026 licensing agreement with Novo Nordisk includes a proposed $300 million upfront payment, contingent milestones and royalties, while Hengrui retains Greater China development and commercialization rights.

BrightGene develops BGM0504, an injectable GLP-1/GIP dual agonist that achieved 19.2% mean weight reduction at its highest dose in a Chinese Phase 3 obesity trial. Its pipeline also includes an oral formulation with positive early clinical data, providing direct next-generation obesity-drug exposure.

AstraZeneca is developing oral incretin therapies through its metabolic-disease pipeline, including elecoglipron, an investigational small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist. This provides early-stage obesity-treatment optionality within a much broader pharmaceutical portfolio, warranting a smaller thematic weight.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Utz concentrates on salty snacks through Utz potato chips, Zapp's, On The Border tortilla chips, Golden Flake and Boulder Canyon. Its manufacturing and distribution model depends on repeat discretionary snacking purchases, making reduced chip consumption especially relevant to branded retail volumes.

Hershey owns Reese's, Hershey's chocolate, Kit Kat in the United States and SkinnyPop popcorn. Its confectionery business depends on impulse purchases and habitual treats, while SkinnyPop and other salty snacks add exposure to reduced between-meal consumption among GLP-1 users.

Mondelez owns Oreo, Chips Ahoy!, Ritz, Triscuit, Cadbury and Milka, spanning cookies, crackers and chocolate. Its global snacking portfolio is concentrated in categories vulnerable to fewer eating occasions, although smaller packages and premium chocolate could help preserve spending per occasion.

PepsiCo combines Frito-Lay snacks including Lay's, Doritos, Cheetos and Ruffles with Pepsi, Mountain Dew and other beverages. Its exposure spans both salty-snack volumes and sugary soft drinks, while zero-sugar beverages and expanding permissible-snack offerings provide partial diversification.

J&J Snack Foods manufactures SuperPretzel, Dippin' Dots frozen desserts, ICEE frozen beverages and churros. Its foodservice-heavy distribution into theaters, amusement venues and concession stands creates exposure to impulse treats and discretionary snacks that customers may skip when appetite declines.

Smucker owns Hostess Twinkies, Donettes, Ding Dongs and other sweet baked snacks, alongside Uncrustables and coffee brands. Its Sweet Baked Snacks segment generated approximately $971 million in fiscal 2026 sales, providing measurable exposure to reduced purchases of indulgent convenience foods.

Campbell owns Goldfish crackers and Snyder's of Hanover pretzels through its Snacks business, alongside Pepperidge Farm cookies and Lance sandwich crackers. Its dependence on repeat packaged-snack consumption creates volume sensitivity, although its soup, sauce and meal businesses dilute the overall exposure.

National Beverage owns Shasta and Faygo carbonated soft drinks alongside LaCroix sparkling water. Its traditional flavored sodas face potential consumption reductions as GLP-1 users avoid sugary beverages, while LaCroix offers an established unsweetened alternative within the same company.

Keurig Dr Pepper owns Dr Pepper, Canada Dry and Snapple and participates in distribution of additional beverage brands. Reduced full-sugar soft-drink consumption could pressure its carbonated beverage business, although zero-sugar variants, water, energy drinks and coffee diversify its revenue.

Flowers Foods owns Tastykake snack cakes and pastries alongside Nature's Own, Wonder, Dave's Killer Bread and Simple Mills. Reduced purchases of donuts, sweet baked snacks and indulgent breakfast products create a potential headwind, partially offset by its healthier bread and snack offerings.

General Mills owns Betty Crocker dessert mixes, Pillsbury baking products, Nature Valley bars and sweet cereals including Cinnamon Toast Crunch. GLP-1 consumers preparing fewer desserts or reducing sweet breakfasts could pressure selected categories, although pet food and other grocery products diversify its exposure.

Coca-Cola Consolidated bottles and distributes Coca-Cola system beverages across its U.S. territories. Its physical production and distribution network faces potential case-volume pressure from reduced sugary soda consumption, though bottled water, zero-sugar beverages and energy drinks provide offsets.

Kraft Heinz owns Jell-O dessert products, Kool-Aid drink mixes and Capri Sun beverages in certain markets. These categories face potential pressure from reduced sugar consumption, but its much larger condiments, sauces and meal businesses make GLP-1-specific exposure relatively small.

Coca-Cola owns Coca-Cola, Sprite and Fanta, alongside Coke Zero Sugar, water and other beverages. Reduced consumption of sugar-sweetened carbonated drinks could weaken concentrate volume, but its asset-light bottling model and low-calorie alternatives substantially moderate direct exposure.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Wayfair operates furniture and home-goods e-commerce platforms including Wayfair, AllModern, Birch Lane, Joss & Main and Perigold. Its CastleGate warehousing and Wayfair Delivery Network address bulky-item logistics. Second-quarter 2026 revenue reached $3.5 billion, with 21.7 million active customers.

Temple & Webster is Australia's leading online furniture and homewares specialist, generating A$665 million in fiscal 2026 revenue. Its supplier-led assortment limits inventory ownership, while exclusive products and a newly leased Melbourne fulfillment facility extend control over high-volume furniture delivery.

Westwing operates a European design-focused home and furniture e-commerce platform combining its proprietary Westwing Collection with third-party brands. Its collection accounted for 63% of first-half 2026 merchandise volume, while digital merchandising and recurring promotional events helped second-quarter GMV grow 15%.

Williams-Sonoma sells furniture and home furnishings through Pottery Barn, West Elm, Pottery Barn Kids and other brands. E-commerce generated 65% of fiscal 2025 revenue, supported by proprietary product development, digital design tools and physical showrooms that complement online ordering.

Lovesac sells proprietary modular Sactionals, Sacs and related seating accessories through company showrooms, e-commerce and retail partnerships. Its configurable seating architecture encourages customers to purchase additional seats, sides and covers, creating repeat transactions around an established direct-consumer furniture relationship.

Adairs owns online-focused furniture brand Mocka alongside Adairs homewares and Focus on Furniture. Mocka generated A$71.2 million in fiscal 2026 sales, growing 22.9%, while group online revenue reached A$209.2 million. Mocka is testing physical stores alongside its established digital model.

Dunelm sells furniture, furnishings and homewares through UK stores and digital channels. Digital participation increased to 42% of fiscal 2026 sales, supported by online ordering, store-enabled fulfillment and an expanding furniture assortment. Furniture is one category within its broader homewares business.

Neighborhood Intelligence combines Overstock and Bed Bath & Beyond online commerce with acquired home-retail brands including Kirkland's and The Container Store. The August 2026 corporate rebranding reflects diversification into home services and ownership, reducing its concentration in digital furniture retail.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Wallenius Wilhelmsen operates global vehicle-shipping networks through Wallenius Wilhelmsen Ocean and EUKOR, carrying automobiles, commercial vehicles and heavy equipment. Its integrated vehicle-processing terminals and inland logistics facilities complement its PCTC fleet, while the Shaper-class newbuilding program expands capacity for automotive exporters.

Höegh operates a specialized deep-sea fleet transporting finished automobiles and high-and-heavy equipment. Its 9,100-CEU Aurora-class vessels feature reinforced cargo flexibility and LNG dual-fuel propulsion, while six additional ships ordered in August 2026 extend its newbuilding program to 18 vessels.

Hyundai Glovis operates a global PCTC network carrying vehicles for Hyundai, Kia and third-party automakers. Its April 2026 deployment of the 10,800-vehicle Glovis Leader expanded vessel capacity, while its planned fleet expansion supports growing vehicle exports and automotive logistics contracts.

NYK operates one of the largest global car-carrier fleets, transporting finished vehicles and construction machinery for Japanese and international manufacturers. Its network incorporates dedicated vehicle terminals, inland distribution and specialized automotive logistics, allowing customers to coordinate ocean movements with destination-market processing.

MOL's automobile-carrier business transports finished cars and industrial machinery through its MOL ACE network. Its purpose-built vehicle carriers serve major Asian automobile exporters, while investments in alternative-fuel vessels and terminal logistics support long-term automotive transportation contracts.

K Line operated 99 car carriers as of March 2026 within its Product Logistics business. Its global routes serve automotive exporters using specialized vehicle-deck vessels, while separate container, dry-bulk and energy-shipping operations diversify the parent company's earnings beyond vehicle transportation.

COSCO SHIPPING Specialized Carriers transported approximately 394,600 vehicles during the first half of 2026, including 333,300 aboard dedicated car carriers. Its growing PCTC fleet supports Chinese automobile exports, while a newly signed ten-year transportation agreement with a Seres subsidiary adds contracted vehicle-shipping demand.

DFDS operates an extensive European RoRo and RoPax freight network carrying trucks, trailers and other rolling cargo across the North Sea, Baltic, Mediterranean and English Channel. Its scheduled freight routes connect regional road networks, differentiating its economics from deep-sea carriers transporting newly manufactured cars.

Tallink operates Baltic Sea freight services using dedicated RoRo cargo ships and passenger ferries equipped with vehicle decks. Its Regal Star and Sailor vessels serve the Paldiski–Kapellskär corridor, transporting trucks, trailers, machinery and factory vehicles between Estonia and Sweden.

home_feed_events.title: Ocean Freight '26: Vehicle & RoRo Shipping - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Kirby operates the largest U.S. inland tank-barge fleet, with 1,134 barges and 291 towboats at June 2026. Its Mississippi River, tributary and Gulf Intracoastal Waterway network transports petrochemicals, refined products and agricultural chemicals, supported by dedicated fleeting, cleaning and marine-service infrastructure.

Hidrovias operates more than 464 barges and 33 pushers moving agricultural and mineral commodities through Brazil's northern river corridors and the Paraguay-Paraná waterway system. Its integrated barge and terminal operations connect inland production regions with export gateways, with cargo volumes sensitive to harvests and river conditions.

TTS organizes Danube freight transportation through its CNFR Navrom subsidiary and affiliated port operators. Its river fleet carries grain, minerals, fertilizers and steel between Romanian ports and destinations across Central Europe, integrating barge movements with cargo handling at Constanța and inland terminals.

Genesis Marine operates inland and offshore tank barges transporting crude oil, asphalt, fuel oil and intermediate petroleum products. At June 2026, its inland fleet included 78 barges and 33 towboats, with inland utilization of 97.4% during the second quarter, demonstrating substantial operating exposure.

MPLX owns Hardin Street Marine, which operated 320 inland tank barges and 30 towboats at December 2025. Its vessels transport refined products, crude oil, renewable fuels and chemicals between Marathon Petroleum refineries and terminals, with a dedicated transportation agreement linking barge activity to refining logistics.

ADM owns American River Transportation Company, whose covered hopper barges, towing vessels and river terminals move agricultural commodities through the Mississippi, Illinois and Ohio river systems. ARTCo also provides third-party towing, harbor services and stevedoring, connecting grain-processing operations with inland freight transportation.

Matson owns and charters cargo barges serving Alaska, Hawaii and remote Pacific island markets, including the 620-TEU Haleakala and 600-TEU Mauna Loa. Its Jones Act-qualified barge operations transport containers to smaller island and coastal markets as part of Matson's integrated maritime network.

Stolt operates inland chemical barges through Stolt-Nielsen Inland Tanker Service, transporting chemicals, biocomponents and mineral oil products along the Rhine and connected European waterways. Its specialized stainless-steel vessels serve chemical customers requiring contamination-controlled river transportation and access to European chemical production hubs.

Enterprise Marine Services operates inland tank barges and towing vessels carrying hazardous liquids and liquefied gases along the Mississippi River and Gulf Intracoastal Waterway. The marine network supports Enterprise's broader petrochemical, NGL and refined-product infrastructure, offering direct but relatively small consolidated inland-shipping exposure.

home_feed_events.title: Surface Freight '26: Inland & Coastal Barges - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Aurizon is Australia's largest rail freight operator, carrying more than 250 million tonnes of commodities annually. Its Central Queensland Coal Network links inland mines with export terminals, while its Bulk and Containerised Freight businesses serve agricultural, mining and industrial customers across Australia.

Rumo operates Brazil's largest independent freight railway business, carrying grain, sugar, fuel and other commodities between inland production centers and export ports. Its Mato Grosso Railway began commissioning in June 2026, initially providing capacity for up to 10 million tonnes of grain annually.

CONCOR operates container trains linking Indian seaports with inland container depots and logistics terminals. Its network combines rail-haulage capacity, customs-bonded facilities and first-mile and last-mile transport, serving exporters and importers that move containers between manufacturing regions and maritime gateways.

Daqin Railway operates China's strategically important Datong-Qinhuangdao coal railway, moving coal from inland production regions toward northern coastal ports. Its dedicated heavy-haul corridor uses high-capacity coal trains and specialized loading infrastructure, making transported tonnage and railway utilization central economic drivers.

PKP Cargo operates freight trains across Poland and neighboring European markets, transporting coal, steel, chemicals and intermodal containers. Its locomotive and wagon fleets serve industrial customers and cross-border corridors, although its ongoing 2026 court-supervised restructuring creates operational and financial uncertainty.

Gateway operates 34 container trainsets connecting Indian maritime ports with its network of 10 inland container depots and freight stations. Its integrated system combines rail transportation, container handling, bonded storage and trucking, capturing rail-linked import and export logistics rather than merely forwarding shipments.

Vale operates Brazil's Carajás and Vitória-Minas freight railways, connecting inland iron ore mines with Atlantic export terminals. Its integrated rail-and-port infrastructure supports large-volume mineral transport, while the Vitória-Minas line also carries third-party commodities; mining remains the primary consolidated economic exposure.

Tielong operates specialized railway container logistics in China, including rail freight, port-adjacent logistics and containers designed for bulk and temperature-sensitive commodities. Its business handles steel, grain, ore, cement and chemicals, extending rail transportation into specialized container equipment and multimodal distribution.

Getlink owns Europorte, a French freight railway operator providing industrial rail haulage, railway-site services and infrastructure management. Its Eurotunnel business also carries freight trucks through the Channel Tunnel, although shuttle transportation and passenger-related activities are larger than Europorte's direct freight-rail operations.

Guangshen Railway operates rail services in southern China's Guangdong transport corridor, including freight haulage and network services for other railway operators. It transported approximately 7.3 million tonnes of freight in the first half of 2026, although passenger and contracted railway operations dominate revenue.

home_feed_events.title: Surface Freight '26: International Freight Railroads - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Waberer's operates approximately 2,000 international trucks and 800 domestic vehicles, transporting full truckloads across Europe and providing Hungarian distribution. Its 2026 fleet renewal program targets 925 vehicle replacements costing roughly €57 million, directly affecting fleet efficiency, maintenance expense and cross-border hauling capacity.

Lindsay specializes in Australian road transport for fresh produce, horticulture and food customers, combining refrigerated linehaul with rural supply and logistics operations. Its nationwide network of more than 60 sites links agricultural growing regions with processors, wholesale markets and distribution centers.

Seino operates Japan's extensive commercial road freight network, combining scheduled less-than-truckload transportation with full-truckload services and logistics. Its June 2026 group data identify approximately 33,068 vehicles, including dedicated linehaul, pickup-and-delivery and charter fleets serving industrial and commercial shippers.

K&S operates one of Australia's larger company-controlled freight fleets, transporting steel, timber, industrial goods and bulk materials. Its K&S Freighters operations combine long-distance road haulage with wharf cartage and rail connections, supported by 22 national depots and specialized industrial transport equipment.

Fukuyama operates Japanese scheduled commercial trucking services, charter transportation and distribution terminals. Its fiscal 2026 management plan targets ¥254 billion in core transportation revenue and includes investment in truck replacements, double-trailer equipment and terminal modernization to improve network productivity.

NIKKON specializes in transporting finished automobiles, motorcycles, automotive components and industrial equipment using purpose-built vehicles. Its 2025 integrated report identified 617 domestic and 209 overseas car-carrier trailers, alongside more than 100 double-trailer trucks supporting efficient long-distance cargo movement.

SENKO operates Japanese trucking and contract distribution businesses serving manufacturers, retailers and consumer-goods suppliers. Its transportation subsidiaries combine scheduled deliveries, dedicated customer fleets and regional distribution operations, supported by warehouses that consolidate cargo into recurring truck routes.

SBS operates a diversified Japanese road transportation and logistics network through subsidiaries including SBS Logcom, SBS Flec and Bridgestone Logistics. Trucking operations handle food, tires, industrial freight and retail distribution, combining temperature-controlled transport, consolidated deliveries and manufacturer-specific logistics requirements.

AZ-COM MARUWA operates Japanese trucking and distribution businesses centered on retail, food and daily necessities. Its group reported 269 domestic operating bases at March 2026 and ¥230.5 billion in fiscal 2026 sales, supporting recurring delivery routes and integrated retail supply chains.

STEF operates European temperature-controlled road transport and food logistics networks, moving chilled, frozen and fresh products between producers, distribution centers and retailers. Its third-quarter 2026 revenue reached €1.45 billion, with international operations growing 17.7%, reflecting expansion of its European refrigerated logistics footprint.

Maruzen Showa Unyu provides Japanese truck transportation for industrial cargo alongside port logistics, warehousing and on-site material handling. Its operations include heavy loads, precision machinery, raw materials and container movements, supported by 190 offices and customer-specific industrial logistics contracts.

CTI operates road freight networks across Western Australia, combining regional trucking, interstate transport, container cartage and local delivery. Fiscal 2026 transport revenue grew 12.3%, supported by higher freight volumes and expansion of its regional network, distinguishing it from nationally focused Australian carriers.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Stolt Tankers operates a global fleet of approximately 167 deep-sea and regional chemical tankers carrying chemicals, edible oils, acids and specialty liquids. Odfjell operates 77 chemical tankers with approximately 2.5 million cubic meters of stainless-steel cargo capacity. Its supersegregator vessels can transport numerous incompatible chemical parcels simultaneously, while its specialized terminal operations and 17-vessel newbuilding program support long-term industrial chemical transportation.

Bahri Chemicals operates a fleet of 33 chemical and product tankers through a venture with SABIC. Its IMO II fleet includes medium-range and long-range chemical carriers serving petrochemical producers, with contracts of affreightment and commercial management connecting Saudi chemical exports to global customers.

Iino operated 33 chemical tankers totaling approximately 1.1 million deadweight tons at March 2026. Its specialized fleet serves international bulk-liquid chemical trades alongside separate LPG, LNG and dry-bulk businesses, providing substantial chemical-shipping operations within a diversified Japanese maritime company.

Berlian Laju Tanker operates coastal chemical and oil/chemical tankers in Indonesia, including the Gandawati and Nolowati vessels. Its fleet handles smaller liquid parcels across regional ports and industrial facilities, serving cargoes that require different vessel sizes and operating networks from transoceanic chemical tankers.

Ardmore operated six dedicated IMO II product/chemical tankers alongside 19 MR vessels at June 2026. These smaller chemical-capable ships carry more specialized liquid cargoes than standard clean-product vessels, giving Ardmore exposure to chemical transportation within its predominantly petroleum-products shipping business.

NYK participates in chemical transportation through joint ventures with Stolt Tankers, including nine large chemical tankers on long-haul routes and eleven smaller vessels serving intra-Asian markets. The partnerships provide exposure to specialized chemical shipping without requiring NYK to operate an independent global parcel-tanker network.

COSCO SHIPPING Energy owned nine chemical tankers at June 2026 through Shanghai COSCO Chemical Carrier, with another vessel under construction. Its vessels serve Chinese coastal markets and international Northeast and Southeast Asian chemical routes, complementing the group's much larger crude-tanker, product-tanker and LNG businesses.

KSS Line operates separate gas, product and chemical-shipping divisions. Its chemical segment transported methanol, bio-oils and BTX aromatics for industrial customers, generating approximately KRW 8.4 billion of revenue during the first quarter of 2026, compared with substantially larger LPG and ammonia-shipping operations.

Dorian concentrates on very large gas carriers transporting LPG across international routes. Its June 2026 fleet comprised 27 VLGCs, including ammonia-capable vessels and chartered-in capacity. Commercial employment through the Helios Pool provides direct exposure to VLGC freight markets and vessel utilization.

Navigator operates midsize and handysize gas carriers transporting LPG, petrochemical gases and ammonia. StealthGas specializes in small and midsize LPG carriers serving regional ports and petrochemical customers. Its March 2026 fleet comprised 28 LPG vessels, including joint-venture tonnage. MOL operates LPG and ammonia carriers through its diversified energy-shipping operations. NYK operates LPG carriers and is expanding into low-carbon ammonia transportation. In June 2026, its subsidiary contracted two VLGCs with JERA for future ammonia shipments from Louisiana to Japan, linking specialized gas-shipping capacity to emerging power-generation fuel supply chains.

Iino operates large LPG carriers and smaller gas vessels transporting LPG, petrochemical gases and ammonia. Its ammonia carrier Gas Innovator entered service in 2024, while an ice-class VLGC began transporting LPG for Borouge in 2026 under a long-term charter serving Finland.

Berlian Laju Tanker operates specialized gas carriers serving Indonesian coastal and regional distribution. Its June 2026 acquisition of the 3,500-cubic-meter Gas Indonesia brought its fleet of similar pressurized carriers to four, enabling LPG and petrochemical-gas deliveries to smaller Indonesian ports.

Samudera Shipping Line maintains LPG transportation exposure alongside its larger container-shipping business. Its subsidiary took delivery of the LPG vessel Sinar Toraja in June 2023, providing an identifiable small-scale gas-carrier operation complementary to its regional maritime services.

Scorpio operates a product-tanker fleet comprising 34 LR2, 42 MR and 14 Handymax vessels as of March 2026. Its combination of long-range ships and smaller regional tankers provides diversified refined-product routing exposure, with commercial employment coordinated through Scorpio's tanker-pool and chartering arrangements.

TORM specializes in transporting refined oil products through a fleet concentrated in LR2, LR1 and MR tankers. Its substantial MR fleet serves shorter regional petroleum trades, while larger long-range vessels connect refining hubs and distant fuel-importing markets. Hafnia's growing minority ownership creates an additional corporate linkage.

d'Amico operates a modern fleet concentrated in MR1, MR2 and LR1 product tankers. At June 2026, it controlled 28 vessels, with approximately 96% of owned and bareboat tonnage using eco-design specifications. Oil-major vetting relationships support access to demanding charter customers.

Ardmore operated 25 MR and smaller product/chemical tankers at June 2026, including 19 MR vessels and six IMO II chemical-capable ships. Its commercial strategy emphasizes complex clean-petroleum trades involving multiple grades and ports, using chemical-cargo handling expertise to differentiate its transportation services.

International Seaways operated 37 product carriers in August 2026, including 28 MR tankers, eight LR1 vessels and one LR2. Its separate crude-tanker fleet diversifies earnings, while six contracted LR1 newbuildings expand its future product-carrier capacity and exposure to longer-haul petroleum movements.

COSCO SHIPPING Energy Transportation operates Chinese domestic and international oil and product-tanker fleets. Clarksons' March 2026 data identified substantial MR, LR1 and LR2 ownership. Its September delivery of the 50,000-deadweight-ton ZHI NENG YUN FAN demonstrates investment in digitally equipped product-tanker capacity.

TEN operates a diversified crude and product-tanker fleet, including LR1 vessels serving petroleum transportation customers. Its charter portfolio includes fixed-rate and profit-sharing employment arrangements, providing product-tanker exposure with a different earnings profile from operators relying more heavily on spot-market voyages.

Navios Maritime Partners owns a diversified maritime fleet including LR1 and LR2 product-capable tankers. Its substantial long-range tanker orderbook, identified in March 2026 industry fleet data, connects the company to longer-distance refined-product transportation, although containership and dry-bulk activities dilute consolidated exposure.

Sovcomflot operates Aframax and petroleum-product tankers transporting Russian crude and refined products, including diesel and fuel oil. Its ice-capable shipping expertise serves challenging export routes, while international sanctions restrict vessel employment, counterparties and access to conventional tanker markets.

Klaveness operates CLEANBU vessels designed to alternate between clean petroleum products and dry bulk cargoes. Its complementary CABU vessels carry caustic soda and bulk commodities. By reducing ballast voyages between cargoes, the fleet offers a differentiated transportation model spanning tanker and bulk-shipping markets.

Teekay Tankers operates Aframax and LR2-capable tankers alongside its Suezmax crude fleet. Its March 2026 fleet included approximately twenty Aframax/LR2 vessels across fixed-rate and spot employment, giving it flexibility to participate in suitable refined-product movements, although crude cargoes remain central to its business.

Buana Lintas Lautan operates Indonesian and international petroleum tankers, including a growing fleet of medium-range vessels. Its first-half 2026 revenue was heavily spot-charter-driven, making MR tanker rates a direct earnings driver, while planned floating storage investments diversify its maritime exposure.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Centrus operates the American Centrifuge Plant in Piketon, Ohio, the only U.S.-owned uranium enrichment technology currently producing HALEU. DOE awarded its subsidiary a $900 million HALEU enrichment task order in January 2026, directly linking capacity expansion to federal fuel-security spending.

Energy Fuels combines operating U.S. uranium mines with Utah's White Mesa Mill, the country's only operating conventional uranium mill. The company produced roughly 1.7 million pounds of finished U3O8 during the first half of 2026 from domestically mined and processed material.

UEC is expanding a multi-hub U.S. ISR production platform, with Christensen Ranch in Wyoming and Burke Hollow in Texas producing uranium during fiscal 2026. Its extensive permitted resource base and existing processing infrastructure make it a direct beneficiary of efforts to rebuild domestic uranium feed supply.

Ur-Energy produces uranium at Lost Creek in Wyoming and began operations at its second Wyoming hub, Shirley Basin, in April 2026. Shirley Basin received authorization for full production in June, with captured uranium transported to Lost Creek for drying and packaging.

enCore operates two producing South Texas ISR hubs: Rosita and Alta Mesa. Its hub-and-spoke strategy adds satellite wellfields to existing licensed central processing plants, giving it unusually direct exposure to incremental U.S. uranium production without requiring entirely new processing facilities for each deposit.

Cameco provides downstream U.S. fuel-cycle exposure through its 49% ownership of Westinghouse, whose Columbia, South Carolina facility fabricates light-water-reactor fuel. Cameco also owns suspended Wyoming and Nebraska ISR assets and 49% of developing U.S. laser-enrichment venture Global Laser Enrichment.

Peninsula's wholly owned Lance project in Wyoming produces uranium using low-pH ISR and has its own central processing plant with 2 million pounds of annual nameplate capacity. The 2026 ramp has faced wellfield challenges, but Lance remains a producing, fully domestic fuel-feed asset.

BWXT subsidiary Nuclear Fuel Services in Erwin, Tennessee manufactures fuel material for U.S. naval nuclear reactors and processes highly enriched uranium. BWXT received a roughly $189 million naval reactor fuel contract in October 2026, giving it unusually direct federal nuclear-fuel spending exposure.

GE Vernova leads Global Nuclear Fuel, which fabricates commercial boiling-water-reactor fuel at its Wilmington, North Carolina facility. GE Vernova is investing more than $50 million there during 2025-26, including capacity and manufacturing upgrades supporting its next-generation GNF4 and BWRX-300 fuel programs.

Boss Energy owns 30% of the producing Alta Mesa ISR uranium operation in South Texas, alongside operator enCore Energy. Alta Mesa gives Boss direct economic ownership of U.S.-mined uranium production despite its larger Australian operations, with Boss receiving and marketing its proportional share of output.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Dycom's specialized telecom construction crews perform underground and aerial fiber installation, trenching, splicing, and network engineering for major U.S. broadband providers. Its established customer relationships and nationwide field workforce make it a direct labor and construction-capacity supplier as rural grant-funded projects move into execution.

Corning manufactures optical fiber, cable, terminals, and preconnectorized solutions used in fiber-to-the-home networks. It reported fulfilling BEAD-related orders for smaller service providers in April 2026, while its U.S. manufacturing footprint and Buy America-compliant product portfolio support federally funded deployments.

MasTec's communications infrastructure operations construct wireline and wireless networks, including fiber placement, underground conduit, aerial installation, and broadband network upgrades. Its ability to mobilize construction crews across geographically dispersed projects provides exposure to the labor-intensive physical deployment stage of rural broadband expansion.

Clearfield specializes in fiber distribution cabinets, optical termination systems, closures, and field-installable connectivity products for fiber-to-the-home deployments. Its modular designs simplify network installation and expansion, particularly for smaller rural service providers deploying networks with limited engineering staffs and construction resources.

Adtran supplies optical line terminals, fiber access electronics, residential gateways, and network management software. Its Huntsville, Alabama manufacturing investment supports Buy America-compliant equipment for BEAD projects, positioning it to supply the active electronics that connect rural fiber networks to subscribers.

Calix supplies broadband access platforms, subscriber premises equipment, and cloud-based service management tools for regional broadband providers. In February 2026, Helexon selected its platform for a multistate BEAD-supported rural fiber expansion across Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, and Michigan.

Amphenol acquired CommScope's Connectivity and Cable Solutions business in January 2026, adding fiber-optic cable, connectors, closures, and communications-network interconnect products. These components are installed throughout broadband distribution networks, while the acquired manufacturing footprint strengthens its ability to serve domestic infrastructure procurement.

Primoris performs communications construction through operations capable of underground utility installation, directional drilling, conduit placement, and fiber network deployment. Its civil construction expertise is particularly relevant where rural broadband projects require extensive excavation, difficult rights-of-way, and long distribution routes between relatively few customers.

ATN operates communications networks serving rural, remote, and underserved communities, including U.S. markets through its operating subsidiaries. Its June 2026 filings identified approximately $101 million of construction grants and $239 million of tribal broadband subrecipient awards, providing measurable government-funded network expansion exposure.

TDS Telecom operates regional broadband networks and expands fiber-to-the-home coverage across smaller U.S. markets. Its existing network infrastructure and local customer relationships support rural and suburban extensions, where grant subsidies can improve the economics of connecting locations that otherwise require substantial upfront investment.

Verizon deploys fiber broadband through Fios and its broader wireline operations. Pennsylvania announced an October 2026 BEAD project involving approximately $28.85 million of grant funding and $40 million of Verizon investment to connect nearly 3,000 homes and businesses in two counties.

Comcast expands its broadband footprint into adjacent rural communities through network extensions and greenfield deployments, using fiber distribution infrastructure and hybrid fiber-coaxial access technology. Its existing regional networks provide interconnection points for subsidized builds that can add households beyond its established cable service territories.

Formerly CommScope, Vistance retained its Aurora Networks broadband access equipment operations after divesting its fiber-cable business to Amphenol. Aurora supplies hybrid fiber-coaxial distribution and access electronics, giving Vistance narrower exposure to BEAD projects using cable-based network upgrades rather than new fiber-to-the-premises deployments.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Clean Harbors performs contaminated-site excavation, soil stabilization, groundwater remediation, and hazardous-waste disposal through its specialized field crews and permitted treatment facilities. Its integrated remediation and disposal capabilities allow it to manage difficult Superfund and Brownfields cleanup projects from material removal through final treatment.

Tetra Tech holds EPA remediation engineering contracts covering site assessments, remedial investigations, feasibility studies, and cleanup design. Its June 2026 Shiawassee River Superfund task order and September 2026 Cross Brothers award demonstrate direct participation in federally procured remediation work under multiyear contracting vehicles.

Parsons acquired thermal-remediation specialist TRS Group in 2025 and developed PFAS soil treatment, groundwater remediation, and firefighting-foam decontamination capabilities. Its October 2026 federal technology validation supports follow-on PFAS cleanup procurement, complementing existing Army and Air Force environmental restoration contracting opportunities.

AECOM performs Superfund remedial construction, site engineering, environmental investigation, and remediation program management. Its AECOM Technical Services subsidiary appears among EPA Remediation Environmental Services contract holders, with substantial recorded task-order obligations, providing a direct federal cleanup channel distinct from municipal infrastructure design.

Formerly Montrose Environmental, Onterris combines contaminated-land consulting, laboratory analysis, emergency response, and specialized treatment technologies. Its ECT2 business supplies PFAS treatment systems, while Enthalpy Analytical provides contaminant testing and CTEH contributes toxicology and emergency-response capabilities for complex cleanup assignments.

Perma-Fix treats hazardous and radioactive waste at specialized permitted facilities and performs contaminated-soil remediation for federal customers. Its Northwest facility began receiving Hanford-related waste in 2026, while an August master subcontract provides eligibility to compete for future radioactive tank-waste treatment orders.

Arcadis specializes in contaminated-land assessment, groundwater modeling, environmental remediation design, and long-term site management. Its U.S. operations address industrial contamination and Superfund-style cleanup requirements, including technically complex soil and groundwater projects requiring engineered containment or treatment systems.

Amentum performs environmental restoration, hazardous-material management, and decontamination and decommissioning work for U.S. federal facilities. Its nuclear cleanup capabilities address radioactive and chemically contaminated assets requiring specialized waste handling, facility dismantlement, and multiyear remediation, creating a separate federal cleanup exposure beyond EPA Superfund.

Stantec provides environmental site investigations, contaminated-sediment evaluation, remedial design, and groundwater assessment through its environmental services practices. Its combination of hydrology, geotechnical engineering, and ecological restoration capabilities supports cleanup planning where contaminants threaten waterways, aquifers, or redevelopment sites.

WSP provides contaminated-site investigation, remediation engineering, risk assessment, and environmental monitoring through its U.S. earth and environment operations. Its specialized consulting teams help determine contaminant boundaries, select cleanup approaches, and manage environmental liabilities at industrial and government-owned properties.

Oshkosh AeroTech manufactures Jetway passenger boarding bridges, JetPower ground power units, JetAire preconditioned-air systems, and airport ground support equipment. In September 2026 it was advancing Seattle-Tacoma's S Concourse modernization as prime consultant and lead architect.

TKH Airport Solutions manufactures specialized runway and taxiway lighting systems, including CEDD contactless energy and data distribution technology. Its inductively powered airfield lights simplify installation and maintenance while enabling individually controlled taxiway guidance, distinguishing the business from conventional commercial lighting suppliers.

OSI Systems' Rapiscan division supplies aviation security equipment including Orion computed-tomography checkpoint scanners, RTT hold-baggage screening systems, automated tray-return technology, and cargo inspection equipment. Its integrated products address checkpoint modernization, baggage screening capacity, and airport security infrastructure upgrades.

Smiths Detection manufactures HI-SCAN computed-tomography airport security screening systems. Its equipment was deployed throughout London Heathrow's terminals in a major modernization completed in 2026, while its August 2026 TSA Level 2AB certification supports advanced checkpoint detection capabilities for American airport applications.

Acuity's Holophane and related lighting portfolios provide high-mast LED luminaires, exterior lighting controls, and infrastructure illumination for airport aprons, vehicle circulation areas, and parking facilities. Airport projects require glare management, reliable continuous operation, and illumination suitable for aircraft servicing and ground crews.

Tetra Tech supports aviation infrastructure through environmental planning, airspace engineering, regulatory analysis, and FAA program management. A July 2026 FAA task order worth $27 million covers airspace redesign, performance-based navigation, environmental screening, and technical support for National Airspace System modernization.

Maurel & Prom owns 40% of Petroregional del Lago, operator of the Urdaneta Oeste oilfield in Lake Maracaibo. The field produced approximately 21,000 barrels daily gross in January 2026; renewed sanctions authorizations provide a mechanism for expanding production and monetizing its existing operating interest.

Eni owns 50% of Cardón IV alongside Repsol and holds interests in Venezuelan oil projects including PetroSucre and Junín-5. Its existing gas production relationships, September 2026 expansion agreements and engagement with oilfield-service providers provide identifiable operational avenues for Venezuelan energy redevelopment.

Weatherford is rebuilding its Venezuelan service presence with drilling, well-intervention and engineering personnel. October 2026 reporting identified at least 20 job openings around Anaco and Maturín and linked the company to Eni's production expansion, making mature-well rehabilitation a particularly direct activity driver.

Baker Hughes supplies oilfield equipment, artificial lift and gas compression technology needed to restore aging production infrastructure. It has recruited in Maracaibo and reportedly signed an October 2026 agreement involving PDVSA, Lindsayca and Fulcrum LNG to reactivate Venezuelan gas infrastructure.

SLB supplies reservoir evaluation, well construction, production systems and artificial-lift technology that can restore output from mature Venezuelan oilfields. Its October 2026 recruitment included positions in Anaco, Maturín and Caracas, supporting a concrete return of service capabilities rather than merely hypothetical market access.

Halliburton provides cementing, drilling fluids, completion services and well-intervention technologies used in oilfield rehabilitation. Its October 2026 efforts to expand its Venezuelan talent network signal preparation for returning activity, although staffing initiatives do not yet establish the volume of contracted work.

GE Vernova signed September 2026 energy cooperation agreements addressing Venezuela's electricity infrastructure. Its grid equipment, gas turbines and power-system engineering could support the electricity reliability needed for industrial and oilfield recovery, distinguishing its exposure from companies primarily drilling or producing hydrocarbons.

GeoPark announced a September 2026 agreement to enter Venezuela through the producing Bare heavy-oil block in the Orinoco Belt. Its redevelopment plans target well reactivation and infrastructure improvements, but the transaction was still targeting closing by the end of 2026 as of its October operating update.

Shell holds development rights with Trinidad's National Gas Company for the Venezuelan Dragon offshore gas field. The project would transport gas into Trinidad's existing infrastructure, potentially supporting LNG and petrochemical operations, although cross-border construction and regulatory approvals remain important prerequisites to production.

Patterson-UTI completed the sale of idle components from ten U.S. drilling rigs for use in Venezuela, creating a documented equipment redeployment channel. Its contribution is presently equipment sales rather than verified Venezuelan drilling-service revenue, so the weight reflects a tangible but limited operating connection.

Tenaris manufactures seamless oil-country tubular goods and premium threaded connections required for drilling and completing wells. Rehabilitating Venezuelan production may increase demand for casing and tubing, particularly in technically demanding wells, but specific incremental Venezuelan orders are not yet established.

Valero operates complex Gulf Coast refineries capable of processing heavy, high-sulfur crude. It purchased Venezuelan crude through newly authorized trading channels in January 2026, creating an identifiable refining and feedstock-sourcing link as exports resume, rather than direct exposure to Venezuelan oilfield investment.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: WSP provides multidisciplinary engineering, environmental consulting and design services for transportation, buildings, energy and water infrastructure. Its global consulting platform integrates acquired engineering specialists and technical disciplines, earning professional-services fees across project planning, detailed design, environmental assessment and construction supervision.

AECOM provides architecture, civil engineering, transportation design and program-management services for public and private infrastructure owners. Its Professional Services operations span feasibility studies, detailed engineering and construction management, while its global delivery centers help coordinate complex multidisciplinary design projects.

Stantec combines architecture, engineering and environmental consulting across water infrastructure, buildings, transportation and energy. Its water practices specialize in treatment facilities, wastewater networks and resource management, while its buildings operations provide integrated architectural and engineering design for institutional and commercial clients.

Arcadis delivers engineering, architectural design, environmental remediation and project-management consulting across buildings, infrastructure and water systems. Its Places, Mobility and Resilience practices combine technical design with environmental advisory, emphasizing complex urban development, asset modernization and climate adaptation projects.

Sweco operates a European architecture and engineering consultancy with approximately 23,000 specialists serving buildings, transportation, water, energy and environmental infrastructure. Its decentralized operating structure combines local engineering relationships with specialist technical capabilities, generating consulting revenue through design, planning and project-management assignments.

Jacobs provides engineering and technical consulting for advanced manufacturing facilities, transportation networks, water systems and critical infrastructure. Following its separation from certain government-services operations, its remaining portfolio emphasizes high-value engineering, scientific consulting and program management for technically demanding client projects.

Tetra Tech specializes in water engineering, environmental consulting, resource management and sustainable infrastructure design. Its technical services include hydrological modeling, treatment-system engineering, environmental remediation and project management, supported by specialized professional staff and the acquired RPS consulting business.

AFRY combines industrial process engineering, energy systems consulting, infrastructure design and architectural services through its European engineering platform. Its Process Industries business supports pulp, paper, chemicals and manufacturing facilities, differentiating its industrial engineering exposure from predominantly transportation-oriented consultancies.

AtkinsRéalis delivers engineering design, technical consulting and project management for transportation, buildings, infrastructure and nuclear facilities. Its multidisciplinary engineering teams support projects from preliminary feasibility through detailed design, while its specialized nuclear engineering capabilities distinguish its exposure to technically regulated facilities.

Oriental Consultants Holdings owns engineering businesses specializing in transportation planning, bridges, roads, urban infrastructure and overseas development projects. Its Oriental Consultants Global subsidiary undertakes international engineering assignments, including design and project supervision for infrastructure financed by governments and development institutions.

CTI Engineering provides civil engineering consulting for river systems, dams, roads, bridges and disaster-prevention infrastructure. Its specialized hydraulic and geotechnical capabilities support Japanese public-sector infrastructure planning, particularly flood mitigation, river engineering and resilient civil works.

Willdan provides energy engineering, utility planning, grid modeling and municipal infrastructure consulting. Its Engineering and Consulting segment serves local governments through civil design, building inspections and construction management, while its Energy segment delivers technical assessments and implementation services for utility customers.

Bowman provides civil engineering, surveying, transportation design, geospatial services and construction management for infrastructure and development projects. Its acquisition-driven regional engineering network serves utilities, government agencies and private developers. Its announced August 2026 acquisition by Bernhard Capital remains an important pending corporate action.

E・J Holdings operates Japanese infrastructure engineering consultancies specializing in roads, bridges, rivers, geotechnical surveys and disaster prevention. Its engineering subsidiaries support planning, structural investigation, detailed design and infrastructure rehabilitation for public agencies, providing concentrated exposure to Japan's civil engineering consulting market.

Worley supplies engineering, front-end design and project-management services for energy, chemicals and industrial facilities. Its expertise spans LNG processing plants, refining, hydrogen and industrial decarbonization projects, emphasizing technical design and owner-side project services within a broader engineering and EPCM business.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Maximus administers government health and human services programs, including Medicaid eligibility, managed-care enrollment, disability assessments and citizen contact centers. Its independent Medicaid enrollment broker services help beneficiaries select health plans, while its operating teams and technology platforms handle ongoing government-mandated administrative workflows.

Conduent operates government Medicaid claims processing, eligibility systems, child-support administration and benefit payment infrastructure. Its government solutions support millions of program recipients, including state child-support disbursement units and Medicaid management systems, combining high-volume transaction processing with ongoing agency service contracts.

Capita operates outsourced public-sector administration and pension services for UK government clients. It assumed administration of the Civil Service Pension Scheme in December 2025, handling retirement calculations and member cases; significant service backlogs and contractual penalties illustrate the execution risks of transferring complex public workflows.

Serco operates public services for governments across immigration, justice, healthcare and citizen support. Its contracts include asylum accommodation, correctional facilities and North American Medicare-related case management, with contract volumes and government policy directly determining staffing needs and operational revenue.

ICF administers government grant and disaster-recovery programs, supporting application reviews, recipient eligibility, compliance monitoring and fund disbursement oversight. Its grantTRAX and disasTRAX tools support federally funded recovery programs, including HUD housing assistance and FEMA-related projects across U.S. states and territories.

TTEC operates outsourced citizen-service and public-health contact centers for government agencies, including multilingual support for health benefit exchanges. Its staffing, conversational technology and workflow automation help agencies manage enrollment questions, constituent communications and fluctuating service volumes without operating those centers internally.

Sopra Steria provides public-administration operations and systems services to European government agencies, including pensions and social security institutions. Its UK subsidiary administers Ministry of Defence pension services, combining case-processing obligations with digital systems that calculate and communicate benefit entitlements.

CGI provides managed IT and business-process services to government agencies, including modernization of benefits, tax and public-administration systems. Its government technology operations support transaction processing and long-running agency workflows, although broader systems integration and consulting dilute exposure to direct program administration.

Kainos develops and operates digital services used by UK government departments, including citizen-facing applications and administrative workflows. Its digital transformation teams modernize legacy public-service processes and maintain digital delivery capabilities, making its exposure more technology-oriented than labor-intensive benefit administration.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: FUCHS specializes in lubricants and related services across industrial machinery, metal processing and specialized applications. Its portfolio includes RENOLIN hydraulic fluids, ECOCOOL metalworking products and CASSIDA food-grade lubricants. More than 10,000 products and application-specific formulations distinguish it from commodity lubricant suppliers.

Quaker Houghton supplies specialized process fluids to steel mills, aluminum producers and precision manufacturers. Its portfolio spans metal removal, rolling lubricants, hydraulic fluids and corrosion control. Metal removal and rolling lubricants represented 19.0% and 18.3% of 2025 revenue, respectively, while Fluidcare provides chemical management services.

Yushiro manufactures metalworking oils and fluids used in machining, forming and other industrial production processes. The company reports a leading Asian market position in metalworking fluids, supported by longstanding relationships with Japanese manufacturers and specialized formulations designed for demanding production environments.

Savita manufactures transformer oils, white oils and specialty lubricants through facilities in Maharashtra and Silvassa. Its product portfolio includes compressor oils, chain lubricants and specialty formulated products. Transformer insulating fluids differentiate its exposure by linking specialty-oil manufacturing to electrical equipment applications.

Panama Petrochem produces industrial oils and greases, textile lubricants, rubber processing oils, transformer oils and drilling fluids. Its specialized petroleum derivatives serve numerous industrial production processes, including textile manufacturing and rubber processing, providing exposure beyond conventional machinery lubrication.

Gandhar manufactures specialty oils under its Divyol brand, including white oils, industrial lubricants, transformer oils and rubber processing oils. Its pharmaceutical and healthcare-grade white oils distinguish its portfolio from conventional lubricant formulators, while its Texol operations extend international specialty-oil manufacturing.

Gulf Oil manufactures industrial hydraulic oils, gear lubricants, greases and metalworking fluids, supported by manufacturing and research facilities in India. Its industrial business serves manufacturing, mining, infrastructure and equipment customers through direct relationships and distributors, alongside a substantial automotive lubricant franchise.

APAR manufactures industrial lubricants including hydraulic oils, turbine oils, compressor oils, refrigeration oils and machinery lubricants under brands including POWEROIL. Its range exceeds 150 BIS-certified grades, while its separately operated conductors and cable businesses make lubricants a diversified industrial exposure.

Veedol manufactures automotive and industrial lubricants, with research facilities at Turbhe focused on tribology and Oragadam focused on grease development. Its specialty formulations include advanced hydraulic oils and industrial greases, supported by OEM-oriented product development and an established Indian distribution network.

Castrol India manufactures and markets lubricants serving automotive and industrial applications. Its industrial portfolio leverages established Castrol formulation technology and distribution relationships, while the broader business remains predominantly associated with vehicle lubricants, reducing its concentration in specialized industrial process fluids.

Idemitsu manufactures industrial lubricants through its Daphne product families, including cutting oils, hydraulic fluids, heat-treatment oils and machine-tool lubricants. Its technical specialists support industrial customers in optimizing operating conditions, although refining and broader petroleum operations dominate its consolidated economic exposure.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: NVIDIA designs GeForce graphics processors and Blackwell-based datacenter GPUs used for gaming, AI training, inference and scientific computing. Its CUDA programming environment, networking integration and extensive optimized software libraries differentiate its GPUs from competing hardware architectures and underpin enterprise deployment.

AMD competes across Radeon gaming GPUs, Radeon Pro workstation graphics and Instinct datacenter accelerators. Its ROCm software stack supports GPU computing outside CUDA, while its CPU and GPU portfolio enables combined server platforms and heterogeneous computing deployments.

Moore Threads develops China's MUSA GPU architecture spanning graphics rendering, general-purpose computing and AI acceleration. Unlike compute-only accelerators, its full-function GPU approach targets desktop graphics, professional visualization and datacenter workloads, supported by its own driver and developer software ecosystem.

MetaX develops domestically designed GPGPU processors and associated computing platforms for AI training, inference and high-performance computing. Its accelerator-oriented architecture and software environment target Chinese datacenter operators seeking alternatives to imported processors and proprietary foreign computing stacks.

Biren designs BR-series general-purpose GPU accelerators for large AI models and high-performance computing. Its proprietary BIRENSUPA software platform integrates GPU hardware, AI development tools and cluster optimization, distinguishing its offering through an emphasis on deploying GPUs in large-scale computing systems.

Enflame develops cloud-oriented GPU computing products for AI training and inference, supported by its proprietary software environment. Its chips and accelerator systems focus on datacenter AI workloads rather than consumer graphics, with product development aimed at expanding domestic large-model computing infrastructure.

Jingjia Micro develops proprietary JM-series graphics processors originally serving specialized aerospace and defense display systems. Its JM11 series extends into desktop graphics, cloud rendering and workstations, providing distinctly graphics-focused domestic GPU exposure rather than exclusively AI-oriented acceleration.

Intel designs integrated graphics processors for Core CPUs and discrete Arc GPUs for gaming and professional computing. Its Xe graphics architecture also underpins selected datacenter products, giving Intel a route to GPU adoption through its large existing PC processor ecosystem.

Qualcomm develops Adreno graphics architectures integrated into Snapdragon mobile and PC processors. Its GPUs are optimized for power-constrained devices, gaming, graphics APIs and heterogeneous computing, distinguishing its exposure from datacenter accelerators through smartphone and connected-device volumes.

Samsung develops Exynos processors incorporating Xclipse graphics technology derived from AMD's Radeon architecture. Its GPU work targets mobile graphics performance and hardware-accelerated visual features, making Samsung a distinct integrated-device GPU developer despite its broader semiconductor and electronics businesses.

Apple develops proprietary integrated GPUs within its A-series and M-series processors for iPhones, iPads and Macs. Its Metal graphics and compute framework enables hardware-software optimization, while unified memory architecture supports demanding graphics and compute workloads across Apple's tightly controlled device ecosystem.

Arm licenses Mali and Immortalis graphics processor intellectual property to semiconductor designers building mobile and embedded chips. Rather than selling finished GPUs, it monetizes reusable graphics architectures and associated software support through licensing and royalties across multiple customer platforms.

Loongson develops LG-series domestic graphics processing technology alongside its LoongArch CPU architecture. Its LG100 and LG200 graphics designs address sovereign desktop and embedded computing requirements, with continuing GPU platform development aimed at broader graphics functionality and compute capabilities.
