holdings_preview.ticker_note: Albemarle combines Chilean Salar de Atacama brine production with Australian hard-rock resources, including its 49% Greenbushes interest and Wodgina joint venture. Its lithium conversion facilities manufacture battery-grade carbonate and hydroxide, giving the company exposure to both resource extraction and chemical processing.

Ganfeng integrates lithium mining interests, refining and lithium-metal production. Its upstream portfolio includes Australia's Mount Marion, Mali's Goulamina and Argentina's Cauchari-Olaroz and Mariana projects. The combination of hard-rock and brine feedstocks supports its diversified lithium carbonate, hydroxide and specialty lithium businesses.

SQM produces lithium carbonate and hydroxide from brines in Chile's Salar de Atacama, with production now operating through the NovaAndino Litio partnership with Codelco. Established evaporation infrastructure, extensive salar resources and downstream chemical facilities distinguish its large-scale South American lithium operations.

Tianqi holds a major economic interest in Australia's Greenbushes spodumene operation through its joint venture with IGO, alongside lithium conversion capacity in China and Australia. Its substantial interest in SQM adds indirect exposure to Chilean brine production, creating an unusually concentrated portfolio of major lithium resources.

PLS operates the Pilgangoora hard-rock lithium complex in Western Australia's Pilbara region, including expanded processing capacity from its P1000 project. Its operating model centers on spodumene concentrate production, while the Colina project in Brazil provides a separate prospective source of future lithium supply.

Rio Tinto acquired Arcadium Lithium in March 2025, adding the operating Olaroz and Fenix brine businesses, lithium chemical conversion facilities and major development projects. Its Rincon investment in Argentina and majority ownership of Canada's Nemaska Lithium broaden its planned integrated resource-to-hydroxide production network.

Lithium Argentina owns 44.8% of the operating Cauchari-Olaroz brine project in Jujuy, Argentina, alongside Ganfeng and provincial partner JEMSE. Its planned Stage 2 expansion incorporates adsorption-based direct lithium extraction, while the Pastos Grandes basin provides additional development opportunities.

Mineral Resources owns substantial Australian hard-rock lithium interests, including Mount Marion and its 50% Wodgina joint venture with Albemarle, alongside Bald Hill. Its ownership of mining infrastructure and processing operations creates lithium concentrate exposure within a diversified mining-services and iron-ore business.

Chengxin manufactures lithium salts through refining operations in Sichuan and Indonesia, including its 60,000-tonne Indonesian conversion facility. Its integrated approach combines upstream resource interests with battery-grade lithium chemical production, making conversion capacity and dependable spodumene feedstock central to its operating economics.

IGO holds a 49% interest in the Tianqi Lithium Energy Australia venture, providing indirect ownership of Greenbushes and exposure to the Kwinana lithium hydroxide refinery. Greenbushes produced 1.41 million tonnes of spodumene concentrate in fiscal 2026, while IGO's separate nickel assets diversify its earnings.

Liontown operates the Kathleen Valley lithium project in Western Australia, producing spodumene concentrate from a large hard-rock resource. Its integrated underground mining and processing development, together with long-term customer offtake relationships, differentiates the project from mature open-pit producers and stand-alone chemical refiners.

Elevra was formed from the combination of Piedmont Lithium and Sayona Mining and operates the North American Lithium mine and concentrator in Québec. Its additional assets include Canadian development projects and interests in lithium resources in Ghana and the United States, extending its potential production footprint.

Sigma Lithium operates the Grota do Cirilo hard-rock lithium complex in Minas Gerais, Brazil. Its production process emphasizes high-purity spodumene concentrate and dry-stacking of processed tailings, establishing a distinct Brazilian source of lithium feedstock for international battery-materials supply chains.

Eramet operates the Centenario-Ratones direct lithium extraction plant in Argentina, designed for 24,000 tonnes of annual lithium carbonate capacity. Its first industrial DLE operation produced approximately 6,700 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2025, while a proposed expansion would add 11,000 tonnes of capacity.

Vulcan is developing the Lionheart lithium and geothermal project in Germany's Upper Rhine Valley, targeting 24,000 tonnes of annual lithium hydroxide capacity. Its proprietary VULSORB adsorption material supports direct lithium extraction from geothermal brines, with commercial lithium production targeted for the second half of 2028.

Lithium Americas is developing the Thacker Pass claystone lithium project in Nevada with strategic participation from General Motors. Its planned integrated mining and lithium carbonate processing complex targets domestic battery-material supply, but remains in construction rather than contributing established commercial lithium production.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Infineon operates major European semiconductor fabs in Dresden, Villach and Regensburg, producing power, analog and mixed-signal devices. Its Dresden Smart Power Fab expansion strengthens 300mm manufacturing capacity, while its 10% ESMC ownership connects the company to additional European automotive and industrial foundry capacity.

STMicroelectronics manufactures chips at Crolles, Agrate, Catania and other European facilities. Its investments span 300mm FD-SOI manufacturing and an integrated silicon-carbide campus in Italy, combining substrates, device fabrication and power modules for automotive and industrial applications.

GlobalFoundries operates its Fab 1 manufacturing complex in Dresden, supplying differentiated CMOS, FD-SOI and specialty semiconductor technologies. Its SPRINT expansion targets additional 300mm wafer capacity, strengthening European production for automotive, industrial, communications and security-sensitive applications requiring qualified regional manufacturing.

TSMC owns 70% of European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the Dresden joint venture developing a 300mm foundry using 28/22nm planar CMOS and 16/12nm FinFET technologies. The project transfers established TSMC manufacturing processes to Europe, with initial production targeted for 2028 rather than currently operational.

Intel operates advanced semiconductor fabrication facilities at Leixlip, Ireland, manufacturing processors using Intel 4 and Intel 3 technologies. Its July 2026 announcement of €5 billion in additional investment targets production expansion, equipment installation and continued development of advanced European logic manufacturing capacity.

onsemi operates semiconductor manufacturing and silicon-wafer processing facilities in Rožnov, Czechia. Its planned €1.64 billion integrated silicon-carbide facility received European Commission state-aid approval in November 2025, supporting regional production of power devices for electric vehicles, renewable energy and industrial applications.

X-FAB operates specialty wafer fabs in Erfurt and Dresden, Germany, and Corbeil-Essonnes, France. Its foundry services manufacture analog, mixed-signal, MEMS and power-related semiconductor devices, supporting customers needing specialized processes and long production lifecycles rather than leading-edge digital logic.

NXP operates European semiconductor manufacturing facilities and owns 10% of the Dresden ESMC joint venture, with rights to corresponding foundry capacity. Its European production and investment commitments support automotive, industrial and secure-connectivity chips, including access to future 300mm FinFET manufacturing.

ams-OSRAM manufactures optical semiconductors and sensors at its Premstätten facility in Austria. Its European Chips Act-supported expansion will establish additional front-end production for integrated optical sensors and mixed-signal devices, creating specialized European fabrication capacity distinct from conventional processor manufacturing.

Vishay operates European semiconductor manufacturing facilities, including its Newport wafer fab in Wales and power-device operations in Germany. Its 300mm fab investment in Germany targets greater production of power semiconductors, with engineering wafers planned for late 2026 and commercial output subsequently ramping.

Tower Semiconductor participates in 300mm wafer manufacturing at STMicroelectronics' Agrate facility in Italy through a capacity-sharing arrangement. The operation extends Tower's specialty analog foundry footprint into Europe, complementing its international manufacturing network with regionally produced semiconductor capacity.

Texas Instruments operates semiconductor manufacturing in Freising, Germany, alongside local engineering and product-development capabilities. Its established European production serves analog and embedded semiconductor applications, providing direct but relatively modest exposure to maintaining regional chip manufacturing capacity compared with its much larger American fabrication investments.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: The Commerce Department acquired approximately 9.9% of Intel through the conversion of $8.9 billion of previously committed federal semiconductor funding into common equity. The transaction establishes direct federal ownership in a major domestic chip designer and foundry operator.

The Department of Defense purchased $400 million of convertible preferred equity and received warrants representing approximately 15% ownership on a fully converted and exercised basis. The investment accompanies federal rare-earth price support and magnet procurement commitments linked to domestic supply security.

The Commerce Department acquired approximately 9.9 million ordinary shares under a $375 million quantum semiconductor research agreement. An additional October 2026 arrangement contemplates roughly 4% further ownership tied to advanced manufacturing, silicon photonics and semiconductor packaging investments.

The Department of War invested in preferred equity and obtained warrants for up to 19.9% common ownership. Federal capital is directed toward domestic tungsten and molybdenum production, processing and capacity expansion serving defense and industrial supply chains.

The Department of War acquired approximately 10% of Trilogy Metals through a direct equity investment and associated warrants. The transaction supports development of Alaska's Ambler mining district, whose mineral resources include copper, cobalt and other strategically important metals.

The Department of Energy received warrants representing 5% of Lithium Americas and an additional 5% interest in the Thacker Pass joint venture through a federal loan restructuring. These instruments link federal financial participation to a proposed major source of domestic battery-grade lithium.

The Commerce Department received approximately 7.1 million common shares under a $100 million CHIPS research award. The issued federal equity stake supports the company's efforts to advance quantum annealing and gate-model superconducting computing systems, including hardware integration and manufacturing challenges.

The Commerce Department received approximately 2.37 million Class A common shares under a $100 million quantum computing research agreement. The equity investment supports work on trapped-ion quantum architectures, integrated photonics and technical bottlenecks in scaling fault-tolerant quantum computers.

Rigetti signed a definitive $100 million Commerce Department research agreement in September 2026 involving federal equity participation. The program targets superconducting quantum computing bottlenecks, including miniaturized readout electronics, expanded cryogenic capacity and fabrication techniques for highly connected quantum processors.

The Commerce Department entered definitive agreements involving approximately 16.1 million common shares and warrants for 17.6 million additional shares, alongside $277 million of direct funding and potential lending support. The investment is intended to accelerate domestic rare-earth mining, separation and magnet production.

The Commerce Department announced a planned $100 million quantum research award conditioned on receiving a minority, non-controlling equity stake. Funding targets neutral-atom quantum computing architectures, optical control systems, readout technologies and error-correction capabilities required for larger-scale quantum processors.

Aeluma signed a Commerce Department letter of intent for up to $30 million in proposed CHIPS research funding in exchange for equity upon final agreement. The project advances semiconductor photonics manufacturing using alternative substrate technologies for AI datacenter communications and advanced computing.

The Department of War announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $1.5 billion that would provide warrants representing as much as 7.5% of fully diluted equity. The arrangement supports domestic silicon carbide semiconductor manufacturing and remains contingent on financing approvals and execution.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: DEME performs capital and maintenance dredging, land reclamation, port construction and complex marine infrastructure engineering. Its dredging and infrastructure business recorded approximately €1.95 billion in 2025 revenue, with projects including the Princess Elisabeth Island caissons and Fehmarnbelt tunnel works. Its specialized vessel fleet supports international project execution.

Great Lakes specializes in U.S. harbor deepening, navigation-channel maintenance, coastal restoration and beach replenishment using purpose-built hopper, cutter-suction and mechanical dredges. Its dedicated dredging fleet and substantial U.S. Army Corps of Engineers contracting relationships distinguish its exposure from diversified civil-engineering contractors.

Abu Dhabi-listed NMDC operates a major dredging and marine-construction platform alongside offshore energy EPC activities. Its marine fleet supports island reclamation, port expansion and coastal development, including works at Khalifa Port and Abu Dhabi's offshore islands. The group's extensive Middle Eastern marine operations differentiate its regional exposure.

Penta-Ocean specializes in marine civil engineering, including breakwaters, quay walls, port facilities, reclamation and offshore foundations. Its extensive Japanese and Southeast Asian project footprint is supported by purpose-built marine construction vessels. Investments in heavy-lift and cable-laying vessels expand its capabilities for demanding offshore construction.

Dredging Corporation of India performs maintenance dredging, capital dredging and beach nourishment for Indian ports and maritime authorities. Its operating model centers on maintaining navigation depths and expanding shipping channels, providing unusually concentrated exposure to India's port infrastructure and recurring dredging requirements.

TOA specializes in Japanese marine civil engineering, dredging, land reclamation and harbor construction, alongside land-based infrastructure development. Its marine engineering capabilities support port deepening, coastal protection and waterfront construction, differentiating its core operations from conventional building contractors and creating substantial domestic maritime infrastructure exposure.

Orion constructs marine transportation facilities, docks, jetties, breakwaters and waterfront structures while performing dredging and underwater specialty work. Its February 2026 acquisition of J.E. McAmis expanded its West Coast operations, adding specialized dredging equipment, environmental restoration capabilities and established defense-related marine construction relationships.

China Communications Construction undertakes large-scale port engineering, dredging and reclamation through subsidiaries including China Harbour Engineering and its dredging operations. Its international maritime infrastructure projects encompass ports, terminals, navigation channels and artificial land development, although highways, bridges and rail construction diversify consolidated exposure.

HAL Trust owns 100% of Boskalis, a major global dredging and marine construction contractor. Boskalis operates extensive hopper dredging, cutter-suction and seabed intervention fleets supporting coastal protection, land reclamation and port development. HAL's other industrial and investment holdings dilute its otherwise substantial marine infrastructure exposure.

Its platform integrates product discovery, payments, warehousing, ocean freight and last-mile delivery, addressing the unusually complex fulfillment economics of bulky merchandise.

Operates online auction marketplaces including Proxibid, BidSpotter and LiveAuctioneers, connecting independent auction houses with global bidders. holdings_preview.ticker_note: Ares Capital finances US middle-market companies through first-lien loans, second-lien loans, and subordinated debt, with selective equity investments. Morgan Stanley Direct Lending Fund holds directly originated loans to middle-market businesses through Morgan Stanley's private-credit platform. Its focus on negotiated corporate lending and institutional sponsor relationships creates loan-level investment exposure distinct from owning Morgan Stanley's broader investment-management and banking operations.

Blue Owl Technology Finance specializes in private lending to technology businesses, particularly enterprise software and technology-related companies. Its sector-focused underwriting evaluates recurring revenues, customer retention, and enterprise-value support rather than relying exclusively on conventional tangible-asset collateral.

Trinity is an internally managed BDC financing venture-backed and growth-oriented businesses through technology lending, equipment finance, life-sciences loans, and asset-backed structures. Fidus supplies customized debt and equity financing to lower-middle-market US companies. Its investments span senior secured debt and equity participation, allowing returns to reflect both contractual interest payments and realized gains from successful portfolio-company ownership positions.

Kayne Anderson BDC focuses on first-lien senior secured loans to core US middle-market businesses, supplemented by unitranche and split-lien financing. Its strong emphasis on SUVs and off-road-oriented vehicles creates differentiated exposure to Chinese family transportation, recreational driving preferences and demand for higher-content utility vehicles.

SAIC serves Chinese car buyers through MG, Roewe, IM Motors and joint ventures with Volkswagen and General Motors, alongside its Wuling partnership. Its mix of domestic brands and foreign-brand joint ventures captures household purchases across economy, mainstream and emerging electric-vehicle segments.

Changan manufactures mass-market cars and SUVs alongside newer electric and electrified vehicles under Changan, Deepal and Nevo-related brands. Its Chinese household exposure spans traditional combustion models and affordable new-energy vehicles, supported by established dealer distribution and domestic manufacturing.

Li Auto specializes in family-oriented premium vehicles, historically led by range-extended electric SUVs and increasingly including battery-electric models. Its emphasis on spacious interiors, family comfort, onboard technology and charging convenience targets relatively affluent Chinese households making major vehicle purchases.

NIO sells premium electric vehicles through NIO, family-oriented ONVO and smaller Firefly offerings. Its battery-swapping infrastructure differentiates the ownership experience from conventional charging-dependent manufacturers, while the broader brand portfolio expands its reach across Chinese consumer price segments.

Roborock specializes in robotic vacuum cleaners and other smart cleaning appliances with automated navigation, mopping and docking functions. Its first-half 2026 revenue reached approximately RMB10.1 billion, with its technology concentrated on automating household floor-cleaning rather than conventional appliance replacement.

Leapmotor manufactures value-oriented electric and range-extended vehicles, integrating important powertrain and electronic systems internally. Its affordable product positioning addresses mass-market Chinese households moving away from combustion vehicles; September 2026 domestic NEV retail sales reached 78,202 units.

XPeng produces smart electric vehicles emphasizing driver-assistance software, vehicle electronics and automated-driving capabilities. Its MONA, P-series and other models target technology-oriented Chinese buyers, differentiating its household exposure through software-defined features and comparatively accessible electric-vehicle offerings.

Supor sells Chinese households pressure cookers, rice cookers, cookware, air fryers and other kitchen appliances. Its established cooking-equipment portfolio is tied to replacement and upgrading of food-preparation tools, with domestic distribution and Groupe SEB relationships supporting its competitive position.

Joyoung specializes in soy-milk makers, blenders, rice cookers, food processors and other small kitchen appliances. Its soy-milk preparation franchise creates exposure to distinctly Chinese home-cooking habits, while newer automated cooking products address households seeking convenience and multifunctional food preparation.

Skyworth sells televisions and smart-home equipment to Chinese consumers through its established Skyworth brand. Its domestic television heritage provides exposure to display replacement and home entertainment upgrades, although photovoltaic and other businesses dilute its concentration in household electronics.

Ecovacs manufactures DEEBOT robotic vacuum cleaners and WINBOT robotic window cleaners, alongside Tineco floor-care products. Its combination of autonomous cleaning and wet-dry household cleaning equipment captures Chinese spending on labor-saving devices; first-half 2026 revenue exceeded RMB10 billion.

Oppein manufactures customized kitchen cabinets, wardrobes, bathroom furniture and integrated home-furnishing products. Its made-to-order production and dealer network serve Chinese households renovating or furnishing homes, making residential completions, remodeling activity and spending on customized interiors central drivers.

home_feed_events.title: China '24: Chinese Consumer Durables - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Tencent operates WeChat and QQ, connecting Chinese consumers through messaging, social feeds, mini-programs, payments, games and digital services. WeChat's embedded distribution supports advertising, transaction services and gaming, making Tencent unusually central to daily consumer engagement and commerce.

Meituan connects Chinese consumers with restaurants, food delivery, local merchants, hotels and leisure services. Its on-demand delivery network and merchant advertising services monetize frequent local transactions, while its extensive rider infrastructure distinguishes it from traditional e-commerce marketplaces.

Alibaba monetizes Chinese consumer commerce through Taobao and Tmall, earning merchant advertising, customer-management and transaction-related revenues. Its marketplace model connects enormous merchant inventories to shoppers without requiring the same first-party merchandise ownership and fulfillment economics as JD.com.

PDD operates Pinduoduo, a Chinese e-commerce marketplace emphasizing value-oriented merchandise, interactive shopping and merchant competition. Its recommendation-driven discovery model and direct relationships with manufacturers differentiate its domestic consumer exposure from premium-oriented marketplaces and inventory-owning retailers.

Kuaishou operates a short-video and livestreaming platform with substantial Chinese consumer engagement. It monetizes attention through advertising, livestreaming and e-commerce merchant services, particularly through creator-led selling and integrated storefronts that connect entertainment directly with merchandise transactions.

Trip.com operates Ctrip, Qunar and other travel-booking platforms serving Chinese travelers. It earns revenue from accommodation reservations, transportation ticketing and packaged tours, making its business directly sensitive to domestic tourism, outbound travel, hotel demand and booking conversion.

Beike operates an integrated Chinese housing transaction and services network through Beike and Lianjia. Its existing-home brokerage, new-home distribution, rental and renovation services monetize major household decisions; second-quarter 2026 housing transaction value reached RMB933.8 billion.

NetEase monetizes Chinese consumers primarily through online and mobile gaming, including its Fantasy Westward Journey franchise and other internally developed titles. Long-running game communities, virtual-item purchases and live-service content create repeat digital spending distinct from advertising-led social platforms.

Bilibili serves a Chinese video community with particular strength among younger users, combining user-generated content, animation, gaming and interest-based communities. Its monetization spans advertising, premium memberships, games and other services, supported by 115.9 million average daily active users in first-half 2026.

Tencent Music operates QQ Music, Kugou Music, Kuwo Music and related entertainment services. Its music subscriptions, digital albums and artist-related offerings monetize recurring Chinese listening habits, separating its economics from NetEase's gaming operations and video-first entertainment platforms.

China Unicom provides Chinese households with mobile connectivity, broadband, communications and related digital services. Its recurring telecom subscriptions offer a different consumer spending profile from discretionary internet platforms, although enterprise connectivity, cloud and infrastructure operations dilute its pure consumer exposure.

China Mobile operates China's largest mobile telecommunications subscriber network alongside household broadband services. Its June 2026 mobile customer base exceeded one billion, providing exceptionally broad recurring consumer connectivity exposure, although the company also serves enterprises and infrastructure customers.

China Telecom sells mobile service, home broadband, IPTV and bundled digital household offerings across China. Its extensive fiber network supports recurring consumer subscriptions, while cloud, enterprise communications and government-related services make its overall revenue mix less consumer-concentrated.

Tongcheng operates an online travel platform offering transportation tickets, hotels and related reservations, with distribution tied to mobile channels and WeChat's ecosystem. Its emphasis on value-conscious travelers and lower-tier Chinese cities differentiates it from Trip.com's broader premium and international travel mix.

China Literature operates online reading platforms and owns extensive Chinese-language literary intellectual property. Its paid reading services and adaptation pipeline monetize consumer demand for serialized fiction, while licensing stories into television, animation and games creates secondary revenue from successful titles.

XD develops and publishes games while operating TapTap, a game-discovery and community platform connecting Chinese players with developers. Its combination of proprietary gaming content and distribution provides exposure to both consumer purchases and user engagement within China's mobile-gaming ecosystem.

Weibo operates a Chinese social-media platform centered on public conversations, celebrities, entertainment and trending topics. Its principal monetization comes from advertising and marketing services, creating direct sensitivity to brand spending on Chinese consumer attention rather than paid subscriptions.

NetEase Cloud Music operates a Chinese music-streaming community built around personalized recommendations, playlists, music discovery and user interaction. Memberships, advertising and music-related services monetize listening and artist engagement, while its independent listing creates targeted exposure to digital music consumption.

iQIYI operates a Chinese online video entertainment platform offering drama, film, variety and other programming. Premium memberships and advertising monetize streaming consumption, with original-content investments and exclusive programming central to subscriber retention and pricing power.

home_feed_events.title: China '24: Chinese Consumer Tech & Services - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: CNBM combines cement and commercial concrete with fiberglass, electronic fabrics, gypsum board and engineered materials. In first-half 2026, its basic materials and new materials segments generated approximately RMB31.0 billion and RMB29.0 billion respectively, providing unusually broad Chinese industrial materials exposure.

Conch manufactures cement and clinker through large integrated production facilities, supported by limestone resources and distribution networks. Its scale and efficient kiln operations distinguish it within Chinese construction materials, while infrastructure projects, property construction and cement capacity utilization drive sales volumes and pricing.

Wanhua manufactures polyurethane intermediates including MDI and TDI, alongside petrochemicals and performance chemicals. Its integrated production complexes supply insulation, furniture, automotive and industrial applications, with process technology and upstream feedstock integration distinguishing it from commodity chemical manufacturers.

Baosteel manufactures high-grade flat steel, including automotive sheets, electrical steel and industrial plate products. Its advanced rolling and coating capabilities serve vehicle manufacturing, electrical equipment and industrial customers, creating more specialized material exposure than producers concentrated on ordinary construction steel.

China Hongqiao produces primary aluminum through large smelting operations supported by integrated alumina supply, including investments in Indonesia. Its production costs are closely tied to electricity and raw-material availability, while aluminum output supplies transportation, packaging, construction and industrial fabrication.

Huaxin manufactures cement, aggregates, concrete and related building materials, with an expanding international production footprint. Its integrated quarrying and cement operations supply construction and infrastructure projects, while overseas plants diversify demand beyond China's domestic property and infrastructure cycles.

Chalco integrates bauxite extraction, alumina refining and primary aluminum production. Its smelters transform alumina into industrial metal used in vehicles, electrical systems and manufacturing, while substantial upstream resources distinguish its cost structure from aluminum producers dependent entirely on purchased raw materials.

China Jushi manufactures fiberglass yarns and reinforcements used in wind turbine blades, construction composites, automotive components and industrial equipment. Its large-scale glass-melting furnaces and specialized fiberglass grades create direct exposure to composite-material production rather than conventional mineral extraction or construction aggregates.

Satellite Chemical produces acrylic acid, acrylate esters, ethylene glycol and other chemical intermediates through integrated petrochemical operations. Its propane dehydrogenation and ethane-based production routes create specific exposure to feedstock costs and industrial chemical demand, including coatings, adhesives and absorbent materials.

Kingboard manufactures copper-clad laminates, chemical products and related industrial materials, supplying printed circuit board producers and other manufacturing customers. Its integrated chemicals and laminate operations connect specialty resin and electronic substrate production, differentiating it from companies focused exclusively on structural construction materials.

Hualu-Hengsheng uses coal-gasification technology to manufacture chemicals including urea, acetic acid and other industrial intermediates. Its integrated synthesis-gas production and chemical conversion operations connect coal input economics to downstream chemical markets, differentiating it from oil-based petrochemical producers.

Angang produces hot-rolled and cold-rolled steel, plates and coated steel products for manufacturing, infrastructure and construction. Its integrated steelmaking operations depend on iron ore and coking coal inputs, while product mix and industrial demand determine margins across its finished steel portfolio.

BBMG manufactures cement, concrete and building materials alongside property development and investment operations. Its Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei cement footprint provides regional construction exposure, although the property business dilutes its materials concentration relative to producers focused primarily on cement manufacturing.

Xinyi Glass manufactures float glass, automotive glass and architectural glass products. Its glass melting, processing and coating capabilities serve vehicle makers and building construction, with differentiated exposure to automotive glazing and energy-efficient architectural products rather than upstream silica extraction.

Flat Glass manufactures photovoltaic cover glass and backsheet glass used in solar modules, alongside architectural and other glass products. Its specialized melting and processing lines serve solar-panel manufacturers, making photovoltaic module production and solar glass capacity utilization central to its business.

home_feed_events.title: China '24: Chinese Industrial Materials - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: SF Holding operates China's premium express delivery network, alongside freight, cold-chain and international logistics services. Its time-definite parcel offerings, dedicated transportation capabilities and automated sorting infrastructure differentiate its model from lower-cost franchise-based courier networks serving Chinese e-commerce.

COSCO SHIPPING Holdings operates international container shipping services through COSCO SHIPPING Lines and its majority-owned subsidiary OOIL. Its extensive container fleet, route network and terminal interests connect Chinese export manufacturing with global trade lanes, making freight rates and vessel utilization central operating drivers.

Sinotrans provides ocean, air and rail freight forwarding, contract logistics and specialized supply-chain services. Its 2025 sea-freight forwarding volume reached 15.60 million TEUs, distinguishing its asset-coordination model from shipping companies earning revenue primarily by operating container vessels.

JD Logistics operates integrated warehousing, transportation, last-mile delivery and supply-chain services for JD Group and external customers. First-half 2026 external-customer revenue reached RMB85.4 billion, demonstrating material third-party logistics scale beyond fulfillment for its affiliated e-commerce retailer.

ZTO operates a major Chinese express parcel network using regional sorting hubs, line-haul transportation and franchise delivery partners. Its model emphasizes high parcel throughput and network density, generating operating leverage from e-commerce shipment growth without directly employing every last-mile courier.

OOIL operates the OOCL international container shipping franchise, including scheduled liner services across major global trade routes. Its integrated vessel network, container management and customer-facing logistics capabilities provide direct shipping exposure within COSCO's corporate group, with earnings driven by freight rates and capacity utilization.

COSCO SHIPPING Ports owns and operates interests in container terminals across China and overseas markets. Its earnings depend on container throughput, terminal handling charges and operating efficiency, providing infrastructure exposure distinct from the freight-rate sensitivity of the group's container shipping companies.

SITC specializes in intra-Asia container shipping and related logistics services, linking China with Southeast Asia, Japan, Korea and other regional markets. Its short-haul trade concentration and high-frequency sailing network differentiate it from global carriers focused heavily on transpacific and Asia-Europe routes.

Qingdao Port operates container, dry bulk, liquid bulk and other cargo terminals in Shandong. Its position serving northern Chinese industrial and trade flows connects terminal activity to manufactured exports, iron ore imports and petrochemical handling rather than primarily parcel delivery.

YTO operates a Chinese express parcel network supported by sorting centers, long-haul transportation and franchise delivery outlets. Its relationships with domestic e-commerce merchants and extensive last-mile distribution infrastructure make parcel volumes, handling efficiency and per-package revenue central operating drivers.

Yunda operates a nationwide Chinese parcel delivery network concentrated on economical e-commerce shipments. Its franchise-based delivery model uses centralized sorting and line-haul systems, making shipment density, competitive parcel pricing and operating efficiency particularly important to profitability.

China Merchants Port owns container and bulk port investments across China and international markets. Its terminal portfolio and associated logistics assets provide exposure to port throughput, capacity utilization and overseas maritime infrastructure investment rather than direct ownership of shipping fleets.

Shenzhen Expressway owns and operates toll-road assets, primarily in Shenzhen and surrounding regions. Its highway concessions monetize road traffic through toll collection, providing longer-duration transportation infrastructure exposure with operating economics different from parcel delivery or ocean freight.

Daqin Railway operates China's strategically important heavy-haul coal transport corridor linking northern mining regions with coastal distribution hubs. Its first-half 2026 coal shipments reached approximately 277 million tonnes, making bulk rail volumes and power-sector coal demand distinctive earnings drivers.

Ningbo Zhoushan Port operates container and bulk cargo terminals serving China's Yangtze River Delta manufacturing and export economy. Its deepwater facilities, large container-handling network and extensive bulk commodity operations make regional trade flows central to infrastructure utilization.

J&T operates express parcel networks across China, Southeast Asia and other international markets. Its China operation competes in high-volume e-commerce delivery, while its Southeast Asian franchise adds exposure to cross-border consumer goods movement and regional parcel-network expansion.

Milkyway specializes in hazardous chemical logistics, including international freight forwarding, specialized warehousing, chemical distribution and domestic transportation. Its handling capabilities and regulatory requirements distinguish it from general parcel carriers, connecting chemical manufacturers with industrial customers through specialized supply-chain infrastructure.

home_feed_events.title: China '24: Chinese Logistics & Transports - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: China Railway Group constructs high-speed railways, urban transit systems, bridges, tunnels, highways and municipal infrastructure. Its specialized railway engineering subsidiaries, tunneling expertise and international contracting operations create broad exposure to complex transportation construction rather than rail equipment manufacturing.

China Railway Construction delivers railways, metro systems, highways, bridges and large municipal infrastructure projects. Its railway construction heritage and specialized tunnel engineering operations support difficult transportation projects, while extensive design institutes and international contracting subsidiaries enable integrated project delivery.

CCCC engineers and constructs ports, dredging projects, highways, bridges, tunnels and marine infrastructure. Its dredging fleet and maritime engineering capabilities distinguish it from land-focused civil contractors, while overseas port and transport projects extend its operations across international trade corridors.

China State Construction combines large-scale building construction with transportation infrastructure, municipal engineering and public facilities. Its extensive contracting network serves complex hospitals, airports, commercial buildings and urban infrastructure, although property development and related activities dilute pure infrastructure construction exposure.

PowerChina specializes in hydropower engineering, dam construction, renewable-energy EPC and water infrastructure. Its experience delivering large hydroelectric projects and complex civil works differentiates it from transportation-focused contractors, while overseas energy development provides substantial international engineering exposure.

China State Construction International delivers infrastructure and building projects across Hong Kong, Macau and mainland China, with expertise in modular integrated construction. Its 2026 projects included Hong Kong's I-PARK2 waste-to-energy facility and modular residential developments, distinguishing its urban construction capabilities.

China Energy Engineering designs and constructs electricity infrastructure, including thermal power stations, renewable-energy projects, substations and transmission systems. First-half 2026 new-energy and smart-energy contracts reached approximately RMB240 billion, demonstrating substantial exposure to China's evolving power-generation and grid infrastructure.

MCC specializes in metallurgical engineering, including steelmaking facilities, blast furnaces and industrial production complexes. Its engineering subsidiaries design and construct technically demanding metal-processing plants, while broader municipal infrastructure and construction activities extend the portfolio beyond steel industry capital expenditure.

China Nuclear Engineering constructs nuclear power plants, nuclear-related installations and specialized industrial facilities. Its nuclear construction qualifications, experience with reactor containment structures and demanding safety requirements create technical barriers that distinguish its projects from conventional power-station construction.

Sichuan Road & Bridge specializes in highways, bridges, tunnels and transportation infrastructure, particularly in challenging mountainous terrain. Its bridge engineering and road construction capabilities address difficult geological conditions, while infrastructure investment in western China provides an identifiable regional project base.

China National Chemical Engineering designs and constructs chemical plants, coal-to-chemicals facilities and petrochemical production complexes. Its engineering institutes and EPC subsidiaries deliver process-intensive industrial projects, including a 2026 coal-to-natural-gas contract in Xinjiang, distinguishing it from conventional civil construction.

Shanghai Construction Group delivers complex urban buildings, airports, transport infrastructure and municipal engineering projects. Its established Shanghai project relationships and experience with dense urban construction support technically demanding developments, while design, foundation engineering and installation capabilities broaden its contracting services.

Sinoma International specializes in engineering and constructing cement production lines, aggregate facilities and related industrial plants. Its turnkey EPC capabilities cover process design, equipment procurement, installation and commissioning, with overseas cement projects providing specialized industrial construction exposure.

Shanghai Tunnel Engineering specializes in shield-tunnel construction, underground transit, municipal pipelines and complex urban infrastructure. Its experience with large-diameter tunnels and underground engineering differentiates it from general construction contractors; its 2026 order disclosures include rail transit, municipal works and environmental projects.

home_feed_events.title: China '25: Chinese E&C - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Hengrui develops and commercializes innovative medicines across oncology, metabolic disease, immunology and other therapeutic areas. Its portfolio includes camrelizumab and multiple targeted therapies; first-half 2026 innovative-drug sales reached RMB8.81 billion, representing 63% of pharmaceutical sales.

CSPC manufactures established prescription medicines while developing innovative oncology, neurological and cardiovascular treatments. Its portfolio includes NBP for ischemic stroke and products from its oncology franchise, with emerging antibody-drug conjugates and biologics extending its business beyond conventional branded pharmaceuticals.

Sino Biopharmaceutical commercializes medicines through subsidiaries including Chia Tai Tianqing, spanning oncology, liver disease and respiratory conditions. Its anlotinib cancer franchise and expanding innovative-drug pipeline combine established Chinese hospital distribution with targeted oncology development and newer biological therapies.

Innovent develops and markets biologic therapies, including sintilimab for cancer and mazdutide for metabolic disease. Its combination of commercialized immuno-oncology products and obesity-related treatments creates exposure to two distinct therapeutic markets, supported by domestic manufacturing and pharmaceutical commercialization capabilities.

Hansoh develops innovative treatments in oncology, central nervous system disorders, metabolic disease and infectious disease. Its almonertinib lung cancer therapy anchors a differentiated targeted-oncology franchise, while proprietary candidates and international licensing agreements connect Chinese pharmaceutical commercialization with global drug development.

BeOne develops and commercializes oncology medicines globally, anchored by Brukinsa, its BTK inhibitor for hematologic cancers. Its international clinical-development and commercial infrastructure distinguish it from China-focused drugmakers, while its Chinese origins and research capabilities make it central to China's biopharmaceutical industry.

Baiyunshan manufactures Chinese patent medicines and conventional pharmaceuticals through brands including Baiyunshan and Chenliji. Its products span traditional formulations, antibiotics and other treatments, while Guangzhou Pharmaceutical's distribution operations provide a substantial route to pharmacies and healthcare institutions.

Fosun Pharma combines pharmaceutical manufacturing, innovative drug development, healthcare technology investments and international pharmaceutical operations. Its portfolio includes oncology biologics through associated companies and conventional prescription medicines, giving it diversified drug commercialization exposure rather than dependence on one therapeutic franchise.

Yunnan Baiyao manufactures traditional Chinese medicines and consumer health products built around its well-known hemostatic and wound-care heritage. Its Yunnan Baiyao formulations, toothpaste franchise and pharmacy distribution combine proprietary herbal-medicine branding with broader consumer healthcare purchasing.

China Resources Sanjiu markets branded over-the-counter medicines and traditional Chinese formulations, including its 999 cold and gastrointestinal products. Its consumer-facing pharmacy franchise and hospital prescription portfolio combine household medicine purchasing with regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing and distribution.

Kelun manufactures infusion products and prescription medicines while developing innovative oncology treatments through its pharmaceutical subsidiaries and affiliates. Its established large-volume infusion manufacturing provides a different commercial base from oncology-focused biotech developers, while antibody-drug conjugate partnerships support innovation exposure.

Shanghai Pharmaceuticals operates pharmaceutical manufacturing alongside one of China's major medicine distribution businesses. Its industrial operations produce prescription medicines and traditional products, while wholesale and pharmacy networks connect manufacturers with hospitals and retail patients, creating exposure across multiple pharmaceutical value-chain stages.

Tong Ren Tang produces traditional Chinese medicines under a heritage brand associated with classical herbal formulations. Its Angong Niuhuang pills and other proprietary products are sold through pharmacies and branded distribution channels, making formulation recognition and consumer trust important competitive advantages.

Pientzehuang manufactures a highly differentiated proprietary traditional Chinese medicine associated with its flagship Pien Tze Huang formulation. Its limited-scope flagship franchise and historical brand recognition create concentrated exposure to premium traditional-medicine pricing, authentication and controlled product distribution.

3SBio develops and commercializes biologic drugs, including recombinant protein therapies and oncology treatments. Its established erythropoietin and thrombopoietin products serve hematology and supportive-care markets, while newer antibody programs broaden its technology platform beyond traditional biologic medicines.

Junshi develops innovative biologic medicines, particularly oncology immunotherapies. Its toripalimab PD-1 antibody provides commercialized immuno-oncology exposure, including international regulatory and commercialization relationships, while its research pipeline addresses additional cancer indications and immune-related treatment opportunities.

Simcere develops and markets pharmaceuticals targeting oncology, central nervous system disorders, autoimmune diseases and other conditions. Its commercial portfolio includes the anti-angiogenic therapy Endostar, while internally developed medicines and partnered assets expand its specialty treatment pipeline.

Akeso develops innovative immuno-oncology and antibody therapies, including cadonilimab and ivonescimab. Its bispecific antibody engineering differentiates it from conventional generic-drug manufacturers, while clinical development and international partnerships provide exposure to next-generation oncology treatments originating in China.

Huadong Medicine manufactures prescription medicines and develops specialty products in metabolic disease, oncology and other therapeutic areas. Its pharmaceutical operations include diabetes treatments, while an aesthetics business and medicine distribution activities diversify the company beyond conventional drug development.

Humanwell manufactures specialty pharmaceutical products, including anesthetics, analgesics and central nervous system treatments. Its hospital-facing pharmaceutical portfolio and specialized production capabilities create exposure to regulated pain management and surgical medicines rather than traditional consumer-facing pharmacy brands.

home_feed_events.title: China '25: Chinese Pharma - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Richemont owns Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels, Vacheron Constantin, IWC and Jaeger-LeCoultre. Its concentration in luxury jewelry and watches makes Chinese high-net-worth spending and gifting particularly important, while jewelry maisons provide a different product cycle from more discretionary fashion accessories.

Swatch owns Omega, Longines, Tissot, Blancpain, Breguet and Harry Winston, spanning aspirational Swiss watches through high-end horology and jewelry. Greater China's watch demand is particularly important to its brand portfolio; Harry Winston recorded nearly 20% constant-currency growth in China, Hong Kong and Macau in first-half 2026.

Kering's Gucci, Saint Laurent and Bottega Veneta brands sell luxury leather goods, apparel and accessories to Chinese shoppers domestically and abroad. Gucci's dependence on fashion desirability and handbag demand creates significant sensitivity to Chinese aspirational spending and changes in consumer preferences.

Prada owns Prada, Miu Miu and Versace, with strong Asian demand for handbags, fashion and footwear. Asia-Pacific represented approximately one-third of nine-month 2026 retail sales, while China remains an important driver of Prada's regional performance and Miu Miu's fashion-led consumer demand.

Burberry sells luxury outerwear, scarves, leather goods and apparel through its Greater China boutiques and international stores. Greater China generated £670 million of its fiscal 2026 revenue, approximately 28% of group sales, providing unusually transparent regional luxury exposure.

Hermès sells Birkin and Kelly leather goods, silk accessories, jewelry and ready-to-wear through tightly controlled retail distribution. Its affluent Chinese customer base purchases both domestically and overseas, while restricted leather-goods availability differentiates its exposure from brands dependent on high-volume aspirational handbag sales.

LVMH owns Louis Vuitton, Dior, Celine, Bulgari and other luxury houses, alongside Sephora and premium wines and spirits. Chinese consumers influence several product categories, from handbags and jewelry to prestige beauty, although the group's extensive global operations dilute China-specific revenue concentration.

Moncler sells premium down jackets, knitwear and luxury outerwear through Moncler boutiques and digital channels, alongside Stone Island. Its Asian luxury clientele is particularly relevant to premium outerwear demand, while high-ticket winter apparel creates a distinct seasonal purchasing pattern.

Laopu Gold sells premium traditional Chinese gold jewelry through boutiques in leading luxury shopping malls. Its heritage craftsmanship and high-value gold designs target affluent Chinese shoppers, with 45 boutiques across 35 premium commercial centers at June 2026 providing unusually concentrated domestic luxury exposure.

Ferragamo sells Italian luxury footwear, leather goods and accessories through boutiques and wholesale partners. Its Asia-Pacific distribution and established recognition among Chinese luxury shoppers create meaningful regional demand exposure, with recovery particularly dependent on fashion relevance and full-price retail productivity.

Chow Tai Fook operates a large jewelry network across mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, selling gold products, diamonds and branded jewelry collections. Chinese wedding, gifting and wealth-preservation purchases drive its business, while premium collections provide exposure beyond ordinary gold retailing.

Luk Fook operates jewelry retail and wholesale businesses across mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, specializing in gold, diamonds and other precious jewelry. Its Hong Kong retail network also captures mainland visitor purchases, making cross-border shopping patterns important alongside domestic Chinese jewelry demand.

Lao Feng Xiang is a longstanding Chinese jewelry brand specializing in gold ornaments, precious metals and traditional jewelry. Its heritage identity and nationwide distribution expose it to Chinese gifting, marriage-related purchases and consumers seeking recognizable domestic gold craftsmanship.

Shiseido sells prestige skincare and cosmetics through brands including SHISEIDO and Clé de Peau Beauté. Mainland China and travel retail are important channels for its premium beauty portfolio, making Chinese skincare preferences and international tourist shopping relevant to brand performance.

Estée Lauder owns La Mer, TOM FORD Beauty, Jo Malone London and other prestige brands favored by Chinese beauty consumers. Mainland China generated $3.06 billion of fiscal 2026 sales, approximately one-fifth of group revenue, creating substantial direct exposure to Chinese premium skincare, cosmetics and fragrance spending.

Kweichow Moutai produces premium baijiu whose flagship Feitian Moutai is deeply associated with Chinese business entertaining, gifting and status consumption. Its distinctive luxury-spirit positioning and domestic customer concentration provide exposure to affluent Chinese spending outside conventional fashion, watches and jewelry.

home_feed_events.title: China '26: Chinese Luxury - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: JD operates one of China's largest first-party online retail businesses, purchasing inventory and selling electronics, appliances, groceries and general merchandise directly to consumers. Its proprietary fulfillment network and inventory-led model distinguish it from marketplaces earning primarily commissions or advertising revenue.

MINISO operates value-oriented lifestyle stores selling household accessories, toys, beauty products and licensed character merchandise. Its mainland network included 4,665 MINISO stores in June 2026, while TOP TOY adds collectible-specialty retail exposure alongside the group's expanding overseas operations.

Pop Mart monetizes collectible characters including Molly, Skullpanda and Labubu through branded stores, Roboshops, e-commerce and blind-box merchandise. Its vertically coordinated intellectual property, product releases and direct retail channels differentiate it from conventional toy manufacturers and general merchandise retailers.

Chow Tai Fook operates an extensive jewelry retail network in mainland China, emphasizing gold jewelry, wedding purchases and branded collections. Its directly operated and franchised stores monetize Chinese gold consumption and gifting traditions, with profitability shaped by gold prices, product mix and store productivity.

Sun Art operates RT-Mart hypermarkets, RT-Super stores and membership-oriented formats across China. As of March 2026, its network included 462 hypermarkets and 34 superstores, providing substantial exposure to grocery spending, fresh-food merchandising and the transformation of large-format retail.

Yonghui operates Chinese supermarkets emphasizing fresh produce, food and household essentials. Its restructuring around the Pang Donglai-inspired retail model makes store renovation, assortment changes, fresh-food quality and customer service central to its ability to recover traffic and improve sales productivity.

Vipshop specializes in online discount retail, particularly branded apparel, footwear, cosmetics and accessories. Its flash-sale and off-price merchandising model connects inventory-conscious brands with value-seeking Chinese consumers, creating differentiated exposure to promotional shopping and branded-goods clearance.

ANTA operates Chinese sportswear brands and associated retail networks, including ANTA and FILA. Its direct retail and franchise operations capture domestic spending on athletic footwear and apparel, with distinct customer segments spanning mass-market sportswear, premium lifestyle products and performance categories.

Lao Feng Xiang is an established Chinese gold and jewelry retailer whose branded shops and distribution partners sell gold ornaments, wedding jewelry and precious-metal products. Its heritage positioning and extensive domestic distribution make it particularly sensitive to gold gifting and traditional jewelry purchases.

Li Ning sells athletic footwear, apparel and accessories through branded stores, franchise distributors and e-commerce. Its Chinese sports heritage and basketball, running and lifestyle collections distinguish its retail positioning from foreign athletic brands and more broadly diversified domestic sportswear groups.

Bosideng specializes in branded down jackets and winter apparel, selling through physical stores, distributors and digital channels. Its dependence on cold-weather outerwear creates unusually concentrated exposure to Chinese winter apparel spending, premium down-jacket pricing, seasonal inventory and weather-sensitive store demand.

Bailian operates department stores, shopping malls, outlets and other retail formats concentrated in Shanghai and surrounding markets. Its combination of merchandise retailing and commercial property operations gives it exposure to urban shopping traffic, outlet demand and store-space utilization.

Wangfujing operates department stores, shopping centers, outlets and duty-free retail businesses. Its historical strength in major Chinese commercial districts and exposure to domestic tourism-related shopping distinguish it from neighborhood grocers and online-first merchants.

Jiajiayue operates regional supermarket networks with a strong presence in Shandong and surrounding areas. Its integrated fresh-food procurement, distribution infrastructure and neighborhood-store format provide concentrated exposure to recurring grocery purchases in provincial Chinese markets.

Hongqi Chain operates convenience-oriented neighborhood stores concentrated in Chengdu and Sichuan. Its dense local footprint serves frequent purchases of packaged foods, beverages and daily necessities, differentiating its exposure from national hypermarket chains dependent on larger shopping trips.

Lianhua operates supermarkets, hypermarkets and convenience stores in mainland China, including retail formats serving urban neighborhood shopping occasions. Its multiformat store network provides exposure to everyday groceries and household consumables, although declining hypermarket sales create substantial operating challenges.

China Tourism Group Duty Free operates duty-free stores selling luxury cosmetics, fragrances, watches, jewelry and other merchandise to Chinese travelers. Its Hainan offshore duty-free operations and airport retail network connect consumer spending to tourism flows, duty-free allowances and premium-brand purchasing.

Yue Yuen manufactures footwear for international athletic brands and owns a controlling interest in Pou Sheng, which operates sportswear retail stores across Greater China. Pou Sheng provides direct exposure to Chinese athletic footwear and apparel spending, although global contract manufacturing represents a substantial separate business.

Yuyuan combines Chinese jewelry retail, heritage consumer brands and shopping destinations associated with Shanghai's historic commercial districts. Its Lao Miao and Yayi jewelry operations provide domestic consumer-spending exposure, although real estate and other activities dilute its retail concentration.

Topsports distributes athletic footwear and apparel through branded retail stores and online channels, including major international sportswear franchises. Its multibrand distribution economics are driven by Chinese sneaker demand, retail footfall, promotional inventory clearance and relationships with major sportswear suppliers.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Daiichi Sankyo originated the DXd ADC platform underlying Enhertu and Datroway, commercialized with AstraZeneca. Its proprietary topoisomerase-I payload and cleavable linker architecture support development across HER2, TROP2 and HER3 targets, giving the company substantial product and licensing economics tied to ADC adoption.

Kelun-Biotech developed sacituzumab tirumotecan, a TROP2-directed ADC licensed to Merck outside Greater China. Its OptiDC platform combines proprietary linker and payload technology, while its partnership structure preserves Chinese commercial exposure alongside international development milestones and potential royalties.

AstraZeneca co-develops and commercializes Enhertu and Datroway with Daiichi Sankyo, combining ADC technology with its global oncology clinical-trial and commercialization infrastructure. The company is expanding these medicines into earlier treatment lines and additional tumor types, particularly HER2-expressing breast and TROP2-expressing cancers.

DualityBio develops HER2-directed trastuzumab pamirtecan and B7-H3-directed elfetabart drozuntecan in partnership with BioNTech. Its DITAC and DUPAC technologies support differentiated payload delivery, while its August 2026 Genentech collaboration extends its platform into next-generation ADC design.

Pfizer acquired Seagen, bringing commercial ADCs Padcev, Adcetris and Tivdak into its oncology franchise. Padcev targets Nectin-4 in bladder cancer, including newly approved perioperative treatment combinations, while Seagen's established linker-payload and antibody conjugation capabilities support Pfizer's broader ADC development programs.

ADC Therapeutics commercializes Zynlonta, a CD19-directed ADC carrying a pyrrolobenzodiazepine dimer payload for relapsed large B-cell lymphoma. Its LOTIS studies examine combination regimens and additional B-cell malignancies, providing concentrated commercial exposure to ADC treatment in hematologic cancers.

Gilead commercializes Trodelvy, a TROP2-directed ADC carrying the SN-38 topoisomerase-I inhibitor payload. Its oncology strategy includes moving Trodelvy into additional breast and other solid-tumor treatment settings, where differentiation depends on efficacy, tolerability and competition from newer TROP2 conjugates.

RemeGen commercializes disitamab vedotin, a HER2-directed ADC approved in China for selected cancers. Its differentiated exposure includes established Chinese manufacturing and commercialization capabilities, development in urothelial and gastric cancers, and exploration of disitamab vedotin combinations with immune checkpoint inhibitors.

Sutro uses a cell-free protein synthesis platform to construct site-specific ADCs with controlled drug-to-antibody ratios. Its next-generation programs include STRO-006 targeting integrin beta-6, which entered Phase 1 in October 2026, alongside work on dual-payload conjugates designed to address tumor resistance.

AbbVie acquired ImmunoGen, gaining Elahere, a folate receptor-alpha-directed ADC for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Its oncology pipeline also includes telisotuzumab adizutecan, a c-MET-directed investigational conjugate, creating exposure to multiple tumor antigens and payload strategies beyond its original pharmaceutical portfolio.

Innovent developed arcotatug tavatecan, a CLDN18.2-directed ADC carrying a topoisomerase-I inhibitor payload. Its Phase 3 G-HOPE-001 gastric cancer study met its primary endpoint in 2026, leading to a Chinese regulatory submission and establishing a differentiated gastrointestinal oncology development franchise.

Lepu commercializes becotatug vedotin, an EGFR-directed ADC approved in China for recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma in October 2025. Its development program includes head-and-neck squamous cell cancer and combinations with its PD-1 inhibitor pucotenlimab, extending the product into additional settings.

Roche commercializes Kadcyla, a HER2-directed ADC using the DM1 payload, and Polivy, a CD79b-directed conjugate used in B-cell lymphoma. Its Genentech organization also collaborates with DualityBio on next-generation payload technology, complementing an established antibody engineering and oncology development franchise.

BioNTech partners with DualityBio on HER2-directed BNT323 and B7-H3-directed BNT324, including trials combining BNT324 with PD-L1/VEGF bispecific antibody BNT327. Its strategy integrates cytotoxic ADC delivery with immune modulation, creating distinct clinical development opportunities beyond its mRNA technology.

Zymeworks develops ADCs using proprietary antibody engineering and topoisomerase-I payload chemistry. ZW191 targets folate receptor-alpha in ovarian and other cancers, while ZW251 targets glypican-3 in liver cancer, extending its platform beyond its separately licensed HER2 bispecific antibody zanidatamab.

Astellas jointly develops and commercializes Padcev with Pfizer, retaining important commercialization rights outside the Americas. The Nectin-4-directed ADC has expanded from metastatic urothelial cancer into perioperative bladder cancer treatment, giving Astellas a direct commercial stake in broader ADC adoption.

Day One acquired Mersana Therapeutics in January 2026, obtaining emiltatug ledadotin, a B7-H4-directed ADC being studied in adenoid cystic carcinoma. The transaction added a differentiated adult solid-tumor program to Day One's existing pediatric oncology commercial business.

Merck licensed sacituzumab tirumotecan from Kelun-Biotech for markets outside Greater China. Its development program evaluates this TROP2-directed ADC across multiple solid tumors, using Merck's oncology infrastructure and Keytruda franchise to study combinations of targeted cytotoxic delivery and checkpoint inhibition.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Legend co-develops Carvykti, a BCMA-directed autologous CAR-T therapy for multiple myeloma, with Johnson & Johnson. Its second-quarter 2026 global trade sales reached approximately $657 million, supported by expansion to 348 treatment sites. Its LB2501 program explores direct in-body CAR-T generation.

Gilead's Kite subsidiary commercializes Yescarta and Tecartus, autologous CD19-directed CAR-T treatments for B-cell cancers. Its established cell-manufacturing network and treatment-center relationships support commercial delivery, while the 2026 acquisition of Arcellx added the BCMA-directed anito-cel program.

Autolus commercializes Aucatzyl, an autologous CD19 CAR-T therapy approved for adult B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Its second-quarter 2026 sales reached $45.7 million, with growing treatment-center adoption. Additional studies investigate whether the same programmed T-cell therapy can treat lupus nephritis and multiple sclerosis.

Bristol Myers markets Breyanzi, a CD19 CAR-T therapy, and Abecma, a BCMA CAR-T therapy for multiple myeloma. Breyanzi's defined CD4/CD8 composition differentiates its manufacturing approach, while expanded lymphoma indications and earlier treatment lines support utilization of its cellular therapy infrastructure.

Allogene develops donor-derived, gene-edited CAR-T treatments intended to eliminate patient-specific manufacturing. Its pivotal ALPHA3 trial evaluates cema-cel in molecular residual disease-positive large B-cell lymphoma, while ALLO-316 targets CD70 in kidney cancer and ALLO-329 addresses autoimmune diseases.

Iovance commercializes Amtagvi, an autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy for advanced melanoma. Unlike CAR-T, it expands naturally occurring tumor-reactive lymphocytes collected from a patient's tumor. Its centralized manufacturing process and specialized treatment-center network are critical to treating solid-tumor patients.

Immatics develops TCR-engineered T-cell therapies for solid tumors, particularly PRAME-expressing cancers. Its anzu-cel program engineers patient-derived T cells to recognize intracellular cancer antigens presented by HLA molecules, expanding target accessibility beyond the surface proteins recognized by conventional CAR-T therapies.

Johnson & Johnson co-develops and commercializes Carvykti with Legend Biotech. Its Janssen organization supplies global regulatory, manufacturing and commercialization resources for BCMA-directed CAR-T treatment, with broader multiple myeloma use increasing demand for specialized treatment centers and cell-production capacity.

CRISPR Therapeutics co-developed Casgevy with Vertex, using ex-vivo CRISPR editing of a patient's blood stem cells for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia. Its separate allogeneic CAR-T candidate zugo-cel uses gene editing to develop donor-derived treatments for autoimmune diseases and blood cancers.

Kyverna develops miv-cel, formerly KYV-101, an autologous CD19 CAR-T therapy for severe autoimmune conditions. Its registrational stiff person syndrome program reported sustained one-year clinical benefits in 2026, testing whether B-cell depletion through CAR-T can produce durable immune-system resets.

Cabaletta develops rese-cel, an autologous CD19 CAR-T therapy for autoimmune diseases including systemic sclerosis, myasthenia gravis and lupus. Its RESET trials investigate treatment without conventional preconditioning chemotherapy, potentially reducing toxicity and making cell therapy accessible beyond specialized oncology centers.

Lyell develops ronde-cel, a dual CD19/CD20 CAR-T therapy for large B-cell lymphoma, in pivotal trials including a head-to-head study against approved CAR-T products. Its GCC-directed LYL273 program targets colorectal cancer, with manufacturing transferred to its LyFE facility in September 2026.

Caribou develops vispa-cel, an allogeneic CD19 CAR-T therapy engineered using its Cas12a-based genome-editing platform. Its strategy uses targeted edits to limit rejection and enhance functional persistence, addressing the durability challenges that have historically constrained donor-derived cellular treatments.

Fate uses induced pluripotent stem cells to manufacture standardized, off-the-shelf immune-cell therapies. Its CD19-directed FT819 entered Phase 2 development in lupus nephritis in 2026, while dual-target FT839 explores simultaneous targeting of CD19 and CD38 without individualized cell collection.

Mesoblast commercializes Ryoncil, an allogeneic mesenchymal stromal cell therapy for pediatric steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease. Its donor-derived cell manufacturing and hospital distribution model differ from engineered CAR-T treatments, demonstrating commercial applications of living-cell medicines outside oncology.

Sana develops hypoimmune-engineered cells designed to evade immune rejection without chronic immunosuppression. Its SC451 program uses stem-cell-derived pancreatic islets for type 1 diabetes, supported by clinical evidence from transplanted hypoimmune donor islets that maintained insulin production beyond one year.

Vertex co-commercializes Casgevy with CRISPR Therapeutics and controls the commercial deployment of this ex-vivo gene-edited stem cell therapy. Treatment requires specialized collection, conditioning and transplant-center capabilities, extending Vertex's pharmaceutical franchise into individualized cellular medicine for inherited blood disorders.

Capricor develops deramiocel, a donor-derived cardiosphere cell therapy intended to treat skeletal and cardiac muscle dysfunction in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Its FDA review was extended to November 2026, while its San Diego manufacturing facility was prepared for potential commercial production.

Nkarta develops NKX019, a donor-derived CD19-directed CAR natural killer cell therapy for autoimmune diseases. Unlike patient-specific CAR-T, NKX019 is manufactured in batches and cryopreserved for on-demand use, with 2026 trials evaluating systemic sclerosis, inflammatory myopathy and related conditions.

Novartis commercializes Kymriah, one of the first FDA-approved CAR-T therapies, targeting CD19 in leukemia and lymphoma. Its established manufacturing and treatment-center network provides exposure to autologous cell therapy delivery, alongside a diversified pharmaceutical business with substantially broader revenue sources.
