holdings_preview.ticker_note: argenx commercializes VYVGART, an FcRn antagonist that reduces disease-causing IgG antibodies in generalized myasthenia gravis and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy. Third-quarter 2026 product sales reached $1.7 billion, while additional studies target autoimmune myositis, pemphigus and other antibody-mediated conditions.

Regeneron co-developed Dupixent with Sanofi, targeting IL-4 and IL-13 signaling across atopic dermatitis, asthma, nasal polyps and other type 2 inflammatory diseases. Its immunology pipeline includes additional antibody programs seeking to address conditions inadequately controlled by existing cytokine blockade.

AbbVie commercializes Skyrizi, an IL-23 inhibitor, and Rinvoq, an oral JAK1 inhibitor, across psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease and rheumatologic conditions. These franchises are central to replacing Humira revenue and illustrate the economics of expanding differentiated immunology drugs into multiple chronic indications.

Kymera develops oral protein degraders targeting intracellular immune-signaling proteins. Its STAT6 degrader KT-621 is in Phase 2b studies for atopic dermatitis and asthma, while programs targeting IRF5 and IRAK4 seek to inhibit inflammatory pathways difficult to address with conventional antibodies.

Sanofi shares Dupixent commercialization economics with Regeneron and has expanded the IL-4Ralpha antibody across dermatologic, respiratory and allergic diseases. Its broader immunology strategy includes next-generation immune modulators, leveraging established prescriber relationships and reimbursement infrastructure across multiple specialist markets.

UCB commercializes Bimzelx, which inhibits both IL-17A and IL-17F, for psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and hidradenitis suppurativa. Its Rystiggo FcRn antagonist and Zilbrysq complement inhibitor address generalized myasthenia gravis, giving UCB distinct franchises in inflammatory and antibody-mediated autoimmune diseases.

Vera commercializes Trutakna, or atacicept, following its July 2026 accelerated FDA approval for IgA nephropathy. The fusion protein blocks both BAFF and APRIL, reducing pathogenic B-cell activity and immunoglobulin production in an autoimmune kidney disease characterized by progressive inflammation.

Arcutis markets Zoryve, a topical PDE4 inhibitor available in cream and foam formulations for psoriasis, atopic dermatitis and seborrheic dermatitis. Second-quarter 2026 product revenue reached $129.9 million, reflecting a steroid-free treatment franchise with differentiated formulations and pediatric label expansions.

Kiniksa commercializes Arcalyst, an IL-1alpha and IL-1beta cytokine trap approved for recurrent pericarditis and other inflammatory conditions. Its business provides concentrated exposure to controlling episodic, potentially debilitating inflammation through sustained cytokine inhibition rather than conventional anti-inflammatory medicines.

TRexBio develops therapies designed to activate regulatory T cells within inflamed tissues. Its TNFR2 agonist TRB-061 is in Phase 1b testing for atopic dermatitis, while its CD30-directed program investigates restoration of immune tolerance in inflammatory bowel disease.

Novartis markets Cosentyx, an IL-17A inhibitor used in psoriasis and inflammatory arthritis, and Rhapsido, an oral BTK inhibitor for chronic urticaria. October 2026 regulatory developments expanded these franchises into polymyalgia rheumatica and symptomatic dermographism, broadening its inflammation portfolio.

Roche markets Ocrevus, an anti-CD20 antibody that depletes B cells in multiple sclerosis, and Actemra, an IL-6 receptor inhibitor used in inflammatory diseases. Its antibody engineering and commercialization infrastructure supports biologic treatments across neuroimmunology, rheumatology and systemic immune-mediated disorders.

Viridian commercializes Lumvoa, an IGF-1 receptor antagonist approved in June 2026 for thyroid eye disease. Its follow-on subcutaneous candidate elegrobart targets less burdensome administration, while FcRn and TSHR programs extend development into additional antibody-mediated autoimmune conditions.

Amgen commercializes Otezla, an oral PDE4 inhibitor for psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis, and Tezspire, an anti-TSLP antibody partnered with AstraZeneca for severe asthma. Its portfolio combines intracellular inflammatory-pathway inhibition with upstream blockade of allergic airway inflammation.

AnaptysBio develops rosnilimab, an antibody targeting PD-1 in a manner intended to modulate pathogenic immune cells in autoimmune disease. Its development efforts focus on rheumatoid arthritis and inflammatory bowel disease, while royalty interests provide additional economics from partnered immunology medicines.

Johnson & Johnson commercializes Tremfya, an IL-23 inhibitor used in psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease, alongside Stelara and other immunology medicines. Tremfya's expansion across ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease extends J&J's established relationships with dermatologists, rheumatologists and gastroenterologists.

MoonLake develops sonelokimab, a nanobody-based inhibitor of IL-17A and IL-17F. Its September 2026 FDA biologics application targets hidradenitis suppurativa, where durable lesion control and comparative efficacy against existing biologics are central to commercial differentiation.

Electra develops ipsoprubart, an antibody targeting SIRPα-related immune dysregulation in secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, a severe hyperinflammatory syndrome. Following its September 2026 IPO, the company is advancing registrational development focused on a defined population with life-threatening immune activation.

Lilly markets Taltz, an IL-17A inhibitor for psoriasis and inflammatory arthritis, and Omvoh, an IL-23p19 antibody for inflammatory bowel disease. Its March 2026 acquisition of Ventyx added oral immunology candidates, including an NLRP3 inhibitor program, to its existing commercial portfolio.

Roivant develops brepocitinib, a TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor approved in August 2026 for dermatomyositis, alongside programs for uveitis and other inflammatory diseases. Its Immunovant subsidiary develops FcRn antagonist IMVT-1402 for antibody-mediated disorders, providing exposure to multiple targeted immune-modulation mechanisms.

ARS commercializes neffy, the first FDA-approved intranasal epinephrine treatment for anaphylaxis. Its differentiated delivery eliminates the needle barrier associated with epinephrine autoinjectors, while a development program in chronic spontaneous urticaria extends its exposure to allergic disease treatment.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Kanzhun operates China's BOSS Zhipin recruitment marketplace, built around direct communication between hiring managers and jobseekers. The platform recorded 70.2 million average monthly active users in Q2 2026 and 7.2 million trailing-twelve-month paid enterprise customers, demonstrating substantial monetization of its mobile-first matching network.

SEEK operates online employment marketplaces across Australia, New Zealand, and Southeast Asia, including SEEK, JobStreet, and JobsDB. Its platforms connect employers with active candidates through paid job advertisements, candidate discovery tools, and matching technology, creating regional network effects from employer participation and jobseeker traffic.

Recruit owns Indeed, one of the world's largest employment marketplaces, and Glassdoor, which supplies employer reviews and workplace information. Indeed monetizes sponsored jobs and employer recruitment products, using its extensive jobseeker traffic and matching technology to connect employers with candidates across numerous countries.

ZipRecruiter operates a two-sided online employment marketplace that distributes job opportunities, recommends candidates, and facilitates employer-applicant conversations. Its AI-powered matching products serve businesses without requiring traditional staffing intermediaries. Second-quarter 2026 revenue reached $118.1 million, growing 5% year over year.

DHI operates Dice, a technology-professional recruitment marketplace, and ClearanceJobs, which specializes in candidates holding U.S. government security clearances. ClearanceJobs' security-sensitive candidate network distinguishes its employer proposition; its second-quarter 2026 revenue increased 14% while Dice revenue declined 14%.

104 Corporation operates Taiwan's 104 Job Bank, a major domestic online employment marketplace connecting employers with professionals and other jobseekers. Its services include job listings, resume discovery, recruiting tools, and specialized career platforms, supported by an established Taiwanese employer and candidate network.

dip operates Japanese online recruitment services including Baitoru, Baitoru NEXT, and Hatarako.net. Its job marketplaces emphasize part-time, temporary, and regular employment opportunities, especially customer-facing and hourly positions. Employer advertising spending and recurring hiring needs drive demand for its recruitment listings.

Visional operates BizReach, a Japanese professional recruitment marketplace emphasizing experienced and higher-income candidates. Employers and professional recruiters use its candidate database and direct recruiting tools. The BizReach business represented approximately 82% of consolidated fiscal 2025 revenue, distinguishing its exposure from diversified HR software companies.

en operates Japanese digital recruitment properties including en TENSHOKU and engage, alongside recruitment consulting and employee retention services. Its online products support job discovery, employer advertising, and recruitment management, giving the company direct exposure to Japanese employers' spending on digital candidate acquisition.

Saramin operates a Korean recruitment platform connecting employers with jobseekers through employment listings and candidate matching. Its Jumpit service specifically targets software developers, while the main Saramin platform addresses broader professional hiring needs. Its specialized candidate networks differentiate the company's recruitment advertising and matching operations.

Wantedlab operates Wanted, a Korean digital recruitment marketplace emphasizing professional hiring and recommendation-based matching. The company supplements its core platform with WantedGeeks for freelance talent and Wanted Space for HR administration, extending employer relationships beyond individual recruitment transactions.

Kakaku.com operates Kyujin Box, a Japanese job search engine aggregating employment opportunities from employers and external job sites. The service monetizes sponsored job visibility and recruitment advertising, differentiating its search-driven business model from Kakaku.com's better-known price-comparison and restaurant-discovery platforms.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: BioCryst commercializes Orladeyo, an oral plasma kallikrein inhibitor for hereditary angioedema prophylaxis. Its acquisition of Astria added long-acting investigational navenibart, while the October 2026 approval of a new Orladeyo pellet formulation expands administration options for patients requiring sustained attack prevention.

Pharming commercializes Ruconest, a recombinant C1 esterase inhibitor for acute hereditary angioedema attacks, and Joenja for activated PI3K delta syndrome. Its leniolisib development program investigates broader primary immune deficiencies, combining acute complement-pathway treatment with targeted therapy for genetic immune dysregulation.

argenx commercializes VYVGART, an FcRn antagonist that lowers circulating pathogenic IgG antibodies in generalized myasthenia gravis and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy. Its specialized autoimmune franchise targets diseases driven by harmful antibodies, with additional clinical programs investigating rare antibody-mediated conditions.

ADMA manufactures immune globulin therapies including Asceniv and Bivigam for primary humoral immunodeficiency. Its vertically integrated plasma collection, purification and fractionation operations provide direct exposure to specialized antibody replacement, with Asceniv differentiated by clinical evidence in refractory, medically complex patients.

Agios commercializes mitapivat for pyruvate kinase deficiency and thalassemia, activating red-cell pyruvate kinase to improve energy metabolism. Its sickle cell disease application awaits a November 2026 FDA decision, while licensed SYK inhibitor cevidoplenib adds a separate immune thrombocytopenia development program.

Pharvaris develops deucrictibant, an oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist for hereditary angioedema. Its September 2026 CHAPTER-3 Phase 3 study showed an 83% reduction in attack rates versus placebo, supporting its effort to compete in both preventative and on-demand oral treatment.

AstraZeneca's Alexion subsidiary commercializes Soliris and Ultomiris, C5 complement inhibitors used in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome. Ultomiris also gained an October 2026 IgA nephropathy indication, extending Alexion's complement-blockade franchise into additional immune-mediated diseases.

ADARx develops onvuzosiran, an investigational siRNA treatment designed to suppress prekallikrein production in hereditary angioedema. Its long-duration gene-silencing approach aims to reduce prophylactic dosing frequency, while its September 2026 Nasdaq IPO created a direct public exposure to emerging RNA-based HAE prevention.

Sobi markets Altuvoct, a long-acting factor VIII replacement for hemophilia A, and Aspaveli, a complement C3 inhibitor used in rare complement-mediated diseases. Its commercial model combines specialized hematology prescribing, infusion-based therapy and rare-disease treatment networks across multiple regions.

Keros' Takeda-partnered elritercept targets ineffective blood-cell maturation through activin receptor pathway modulation. Phase 3 trials initiated in 2026 investigate anemia associated with myelofibrosis and lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes, supporting a licensing and milestone model tied to rare hematology treatments.

Rigel markets Tavalisse, an oral spleen tyrosine kinase inhibitor for chronic immune thrombocytopenia, where immune activity destroys circulating platelets. Its development-stage R289 program targets myelodysplastic syndromes, although its growing oncology portfolio reduces the company's concentration in rare immune and blood disorders.

Annexon develops tanruprubart, an anti-C1q antibody designed to prevent complement-mediated nerve damage in Guillain-Barré syndrome. Its 2026 European regulatory submission and planned U.S. filing provide a differentiated rare autoimmune neurology exposure alongside its separate ophthalmology pipeline

Biogen acquired Apellis in May 2026, gaining Empaveli, a complement C3 inhibitor for paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and rare complement-mediated kidney diseases. The acquisition provides a distinct commercial complement-blockade franchise alongside Biogen's established neuroscience operations and developing nephrology infrastructure.

CSL Behring supplies Idelvion and Afstyla clotting-factor treatments, Hizentra immunoglobulin replacement and Hemgenix gene therapy for hemophilia B. Its plasma collection and fractionation infrastructure supports essential chronic therapies, while Hemgenix adds a one-time genetic treatment with specialized manufacturing and delivery requirements.

Novartis commercializes Fabhalta, an oral complement factor B inhibitor approved for paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and complement-mediated kidney diseases. Its proximal complement blockade differs from C5 inhibition by targeting the alternative pathway upstream, creating competitive options for controlling intravascular and extravascular hemolysis.

Protagonist developed rusfertide, a hepcidin mimetic approved in August 2026 as Mimrylo for polycythemia vera, partnered with Takeda. By reducing iron availability for excessive red-cell production, it addresses the disease's hematologic mechanism. Its separately partnered oral IL-23 antagonist icotrokinra provides immunology exposure.

Roche commercializes Hemlibra, a bispecific antibody that substitutes for activated factor VIII function in hemophilia A prophylaxis. Its subcutaneous administration and efficacy in patients with factor VIII inhibitors differentiate its clotting-disorder franchise from conventional intravenous factor replacement therapies.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: BioMarin markets enzyme and metabolic therapies including Palynziq for phenylketonuria, Vimizim for Morquio A syndrome and Brineura for CLN2 disease. Its April 2026 acquisition of Amicus added Galafold for Fabry disease and Pombiliti/Opfolda for Pompe disease, greatly expanding its lysosomal storage portfolio.

Ultragenyx commercializes Crysvita for X-linked hypophosphatemia and Mepsevii for mucopolysaccharidosis VII. Its Genglycos gene therapy received accelerated FDA approval in August 2026 for glycogen storage disease type Ia, adding a one-time treatment intended to correct the underlying metabolic enzyme deficiency.

Sanofi maintains a substantial inherited metabolic disease franchise through Fabrazyme for Fabry disease, Cerezyme and Cerdelga for Gaucher disease, and Nexviazyme for Pompe disease. These products combine enzyme replacement and substrate reduction, supported by specialized manufacturing and longstanding metabolic-disease treatment networks.

Denali commercializes Avlayah for neurological manifestations of Hunter syndrome, an inherited lysosomal storage disorder. Its TransportVehicle technology carries replacement enzymes across the blood-brain barrier, addressing neurological complications that conventional intravenous enzyme therapies often cannot adequately reach.

Takeda markets Vpriv, an enzyme replacement therapy for Gaucher disease, and Elaprase for Hunter syndrome, alongside Replagal for Fabry disease in international markets. Its inherited metabolic disease portfolio depends on specialized infusion infrastructure, disease-specific physician relationships and long-term treatment adherence.

Ascendis commercializes Yorvipath for hypoparathyroidism and Yuviwel for achondroplasia, alongside Skytrofa for growth hormone deficiency. Its TransCon technology prolongs hormone or peptide exposure, allowing sustained physiological replacement or pathway modulation in rare endocrine and skeletal conditions.

BridgeBio develops encaleret for autosomal dominant hypocalcemia type 1, a genetic calcium-sensing receptor disorder, and oral infigratinib for FGFR3-driven achondroplasia. Both programs target defined molecular defects, while its patient-identification initiatives support development and commercial preparation in genetically diagnosed populations.

PTC markets Sephience, an oral treatment for sepiapterin-responsive phenylketonuria that enhances phenylalanine hydroxylase activity. Its therapy addresses abnormal phenylalanine metabolism through a mechanism distinct from BioMarin's enzyme-substitution approach, with treatment eligibility determined by biochemical responsiveness.

Alnylam commercializes Oxlumo, an RNA interference therapy that silences hepatic HAO1 expression to reduce oxalate production in primary hyperoxaluria type 1. Its Givlaari treatment similarly uses RNA silencing to suppress a pathogenic metabolic pathway in acute hepatic porphyria.

Arcturus develops ARCT-810, an mRNA therapy designed to supply functional ornithine transcarbamylase enzyme in patients with OTC deficiency. Its September 2026 Phase 2 update reported encouraging urea-cycle biomarker activity, while LUNAR lipid nanoparticles enable repeatable delivery of enzyme-producing RNA to the liver.

Novo Nordisk markets Rivfloza, an siRNA therapy targeting LDHA to reduce oxalate generation in primary hyperoxaluria type 1. Unlike Alnylam's Oxlumo, which targets HAO1, Rivfloza suppresses a different enzyme within hepatic glyoxylate metabolism, providing a distinct intervention in the same inherited disorder.

Sangamo develops isaralgagene civaparvovec, an AAV-based gene therapy intended to restore alpha-galactosidase A production in Fabry disease. Its liver-directed approach aims to generate sustained enzyme activity after one infusion, potentially replacing repeated enzyme replacement treatment for patients with the inherited lysosomal disorder.

Rezolute develops ersodetug, an antibody targeting insulin receptor signaling to prevent severe hypoglycemia caused by congenital and tumor-associated hyperinsulinism. Its Phase 3 upLIFT trial completed enrollment in October 2026, testing the drug in patients whose excessive insulin activity creates dangerous glucose instability.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Recursion's Recursion OS combines automated cellular imaging, phenomics, proprietary biological datasets and machine learning to identify drug targets and optimize compounds. Its acquisition of Exscientia added computational chemistry capabilities, while internal drug candidates and partnered programs test the platform's clinical translation.

Insilico's Pharma.AI platform connects target identification, generative molecular design and clinical candidate development. Its TNIK inhibitor rentosertib, discovered using AI methods, advanced into late-stage testing for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, providing clinical validation opportunities for an AI-originated molecule.

Schrödinger combines physics-based molecular simulation with machine learning to predict binding, optimize chemical structures and prioritize compounds. Its commercial computational software generates platform revenue, while pharmaceutical partnerships and internal therapeutic programs create potential development milestones and downstream drug economics.

XtalPi combines physics-based molecular calculations, machine learning and automated laboratory robotics to discover and optimize compounds. Its pharmaceutical partnerships integrate computational predictions with experimental validation, generating research payments, potential development milestones and licensing opportunities from drug-discovery projects.

Absci uses generative AI and automated wet-lab experiments to design and optimize therapeutic antibodies. Its internal candidate ABS-201 targets the prolactin receptor, while additional antibody programs combine predictive design with experimental screening to identify molecules with differentiated binding and functional properties.

Generate's generative biology platform designs therapeutic proteins using machine learning, proprietary experimental datasets and automated biological testing. Its computationally engineered anti-TSLP antibody GB-0895 advanced into late-stage development for severe asthma, testing whether generative protein engineering translates into clinical efficacy.

Iambic integrates NeuralPLexer structural models, Enchant property prediction and automated chemistry experiments into an iterative drug-design platform. Its AI-designed HER2 inhibitor IAM1363 entered clinical development, while pharmaceutical partnerships demonstrate applications across oncology and other therapeutic areas.

Relay's Dynamo platform integrates protein structural dynamics, computational simulation and experimental biology to identify binding opportunities overlooked by static structural methods. Its PI3Kalpha inhibitor zovegalisib uses molecular-dynamics-informed design to target genetically defined breast cancers.

AbCellera combines high-throughput antibody screening, computational analysis and AI-assisted protein engineering to discover therapeutics against difficult targets. Its internal antibody programs and specialized GPCR and ion-channel discovery capabilities distinguish its integrated discovery approach from purely computational software platforms.

Lilly operates TuneLab, which provides external biotech companies with proprietary AI drug-discovery models trained on its research data. Its NVIDIA collaboration involves up to $1 billion of combined investment over five years in AI infrastructure, biological foundation models and automated experimental systems for molecular discovery.

Lantern's RADR platform analyzes genomic, biomarker and drug-response datasets to identify cancer patients likely to benefit from specific compounds. Its oncology programs use computational patient stratification and drug-repositioning insights rather than relying principally on generative molecular design.

Twist supplies antibody discovery, expression and characterization workflows used to train and validate AI-designed biologics. Its September 2026 Lilly TuneLab agreement provides experimental antibody data supporting developability prediction, while high-throughput screening and synthetic DNA manufacturing enable iterative AI-guided molecule optimization.

BioAge applies machine learning to longitudinal human aging cohorts containing molecular measurements and clinical outcomes. Its Longevity Map identifies therapeutic targets associated with aging and metabolic disease, while computational discovery partnerships extend its approach into molecular candidate design.

Eikon's single-molecule tracking technology measures protein movement and interactions in living cells at high throughput. Machine learning analyzes these experimental measurements to inform therapeutic discovery, while its internal oncology development programs test the clinical relevance of dynamic biological observations.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Farmer Mac provides a secondary market for agricultural mortgages and rural infrastructure loans through purchases, guarantees, and securitization. Its Farm & Ranch business had approximately $22.0 billion in outstanding business volume at June 2026, including farmland loans, USDA-backed instruments, and lending commitments.

Nicolet operates a substantial agricultural banking franchise across Wisconsin and neighboring markets, financing dairy operations, livestock, farm equipment, and agricultural property. Agricultural loans represented 16% of its $10.8 billion loan portfolio in June 2026, creating meaningful exposure to dairy prices and regional farm economics.

Southern Missouri Bank provides agricultural real estate financing and farm production credit across Missouri and neighboring markets. At June 2026, agricultural real estate loans totaled $295.8 million and agricultural business loans $219.2 million, together representing approximately 12% of its lending portfolio.

Equity Bank lends to agricultural customers across Kansas and surrounding markets, including farmland purchases, seasonal crop production, livestock operations, and machinery financing. Its June 2026 portfolio contained $419.8 million of agricultural real estate loans and $247.3 million of agricultural operating credit.

First Mid provides operating lines to Illinois grain farmers for planting and harvesting corn and soybeans, alongside farmland mortgages and equipment financing. At December 2025, it held approximately $374 million in agricultural real estate loans and $308 million in agricultural production loans.

Farmers National Bank operates an Ohio-based relationship banking franchise with agricultural lending among its commercial and real estate products. At year-end 2025, it held $266.3 million in agricultural loans, representing 8.1% of total loans, providing exposure to regional farm financing.

HBT operates community banking franchises across Illinois and Iowa, including agricultural and farmland lending to local producers. At December 2025, agricultural and farmland loans totaled approximately $275 million, giving its regional franchise direct exposure to agricultural credit conditions alongside commercial real estate lending.

Landmark Bank finances agricultural operating needs and farmland purchases across Kansas through its community banking network. Its 2025 annual report identifies agricultural real estate loans of $38.7 million, alongside operating credit whose repayment depends on crop yields, commodity prices, and farm borrower cash flows.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Pinnacle's relationship-banker model targets owner-operated and middle-market businesses, pairing commercial loans with operating deposits and treasury services. Its January 2026 combination with Synovus added substantial Southeastern commercial banking relationships and expanded its scale in Nashville, Atlanta, and other business markets.

Texas Capital explicitly targets founder-owned, family-owned, sponsor-backed, and publicly traded middle-market companies. Its integrated commercial and investment banking model combines working-capital loans, acquisition finance, treasury services, and M&A advisory, distinguishing it from regional banks focused principally on retail deposits.

Wintrust combines locally managed commercial banking franchises around Chicago and other metropolitan markets with specialized commercial finance businesses. It offers middle-market borrowers equipment finance, working-capital credit, treasury management, and industry-specific lending while retaining local credit decisions and relationship management.

UMB maintains a substantial commercial banking franchise covering conventional C&I lending, asset-based finance, equipment lending, and industry-specific credit. Following its acquisition of Heartland Financial, commercial relationships account for a significant share of its deposits and loans alongside institutional servicing businesses.

Western Alliance builds specialized commercial banking teams around business sectors rather than relying solely on traditional branch networks. Its industry-focused operations include technology, life sciences, commercial finance, and a healthcare banking team launched in March 2026 for providers and medical businesses.

Enterprise Bank & Trust focuses on commercial clients through relationship lending and specialized teams serving areas such as life sciences, nonprofit organizations, and professional services. Its business-oriented franchise also offers treasury management, commercial deposits, and SBA lending to support smaller and middle-market companies.

F.N.B.'s commercial banking operations serve middle-market businesses across Pennsylvania and its expanding Mid-Atlantic and Southeastern footprint. Its corporate bankers target companies with annual revenues of $50 million or more, connecting credit facilities with treasury management and capital-markets services.

Customers operates a branch-light commercial banking model combining traditional small and middle-market lending with specialized national businesses. At June 2026, commercial loans represented approximately 91.5% of its total loan and lease portfolio, including mortgage finance, specialty lending, and C&I loans.

Old National provides commercial and corporate banking across Midwestern markets, including working-capital financing, treasury management, and business lending. Its integration of Bremer Bank expanded its Minnesota and Upper Midwest commercial customer base and increased the scale of its relationship banking franchise.

Associated serves commercial and corporate clients through its Wisconsin-based banking network and regional metropolitan teams. Its presence in Milwaukee, Chicago, Minneapolis, and other Midwestern business centers supports C&I lending and treasury services for local manufacturers, distributors, and operating companies.

BOK Financial combines general business lending with established sector-specific commercial banking capabilities. Its energy and healthcare lending businesses complement services-sector financing and corporate treasury relationships; energy loans reached approximately $3.3 billion in September 2026, representing 12% of total loans.

Fulton operates commercial banking relationships across Pennsylvania and neighboring Mid-Atlantic markets. Its business lending includes commercial lines of credit, equipment financing, SBA loans, and treasury services, with the acquired Republic First Bank operations strengthening its Philadelphia-area franchise.

Hancock Whitney serves Gulf Coast businesses through commercial lending and treasury relationships across Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Florida, and Texas. Its operating-company customers span regional industries including energy services, healthcare, logistics, and other businesses linked to Gulf Coast commercial activity.

Huntington combines extensive small-business and middle-market banking operations with equipment finance, inventory finance, and commercial payments. Its acquisitions of Veritex in October 2025 and Cadence in February 2026 expanded its Texas and Southeastern commercial lending and deposit relationships.

Frost Bank serves Texas businesses through locally managed commercial banking relationships and treasury services. Its longstanding Texas franchise emphasizes commercial deposits, credit underwriting, and operating-company relationships, while its branch expansion supports business customer acquisition in large Texas metropolitan markets.

M&T operates an established commercial banking franchise serving middle-market companies across the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic. Its relationship model connects C&I lending and treasury services with regional business owners, while Wilmington Trust adds institutional trust and fiduciary capabilities alongside conventional commercial banking.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Bank OZK's Real Estate Specialties Group finances large commercial real estate construction and development projects nationwide. RESG represented 45.2% of total loans in September 2026, down from a historical peak of 70%, as the bank diversifies into corporate and other lending.

Metropolitan Commercial Bank's CRE portfolio totaled approximately $6.4 billion, or 87.4% of loans, in June 2026. Skilled nursing facilities alone accounted for roughly 42% of loans, creating unusually concentrated exposure to healthcare real estate financing and operator creditworthiness.

NorthEast Community Bancorp specializes in construction financing across the New York metropolitan region, particularly Rockland, Orange, Sullivan, and Bronx counties. Construction loans represented 71.8% of total loans at year-end 2025, making project completion and local development conditions central to its banking economics.

Dime's multifamily and non-owner-occupied CRE loans represented approximately 55% of its June 2026 loan book. Its New York City apartment portfolio includes rent-regulated and free-market properties, making local housing regulation, refinancing economics, and rental-property valuations especially important.

OceanFirst reported $9.13 billion in investor-owned CRE, multifamily, and construction loans, representing 56.1% of total loans in June 2026. Its acquisition of Flushing Financial expanded its New York property lending portfolio, although it subsequently sold $1.31 billion of acquired multifamily loans.

Valley National held approximately $27.9 billion of commercial real estate loans and $2.5 billion of construction loans in June 2026. Its New Jersey, New York, and Florida lending relationships include multifamily and owner-occupied properties, while its non-owner-occupied CRE concentration remained elevated relative to regulatory capital.

ConnectOne Bank has substantial commercial real estate exposure across New Jersey and metropolitan New York. Its combined franchise following the First of Long Island merger carried approximately $7.1 billion in CRE loans in June 2026, linking earnings to regional property lending and refinancing activity.

Flagstar retains one of the largest multifamily banking portfolios in the United States, with approximately $26.9 billion outstanding in June 2026. Its New York apartment exposure, including rent-regulated housing, remains material even as management reduces legacy concentrations and repositions the bank.

Kearny held approximately $2.5 billion in multifamily mortgages and $1.0 billion in nonresidential property loans in June 2026, together representing nearly 60% of total loans. Its lending primarily finances apartment buildings, mixed-use properties, and commercial real estate across New Jersey and neighboring markets.

Columbia's expanded Western U.S. franchise includes substantial commercial property exposure following its Pacific Premier combination. In March 2026, multifamily represented 21% of loans, non-owner-occupied CRE 17%, and owner-occupied CRE another 15%, spanning California and Pacific Northwest property markets.

BankUnited maintains a diversified commercial property portfolio across Florida, New York, and other markets, including office, industrial, multifamily, retail, and hotels. Its September 2026 disclosures show a substantial office component, though management has increasingly emphasized commercial and industrial lending over CRE concentration.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Nubank operates a branchless digital financial platform across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, reaching 139 million customers by June 2026. Its mobile distribution, proprietary underwriting models, and low operating-cost structure support credit cards, deposits, personal loans, and expanding primary banking relationships.

SoFi combines a nationally chartered digital bank with consumer lending, investing, payments, and financial planning products in one application. Its 15.8 million members and $45.5 billion in deposits at June 2026 demonstrate its ability to convert digital customer acquisition into funded banking relationships.

Axos operates a branchless banking franchise offering consumer deposits, commercial lending, securities-backed loans, and specialized institutional accounts. Its May 2026 acquisition of Jenius Bank added approximately $2.3 billion in deposits, expanding its digital funding base and consumer banking capabilities.

Ally Bank gathers retail deposits through online channels without operating a traditional branch network, funding a large automotive lending franchise. Deposits represented 88% of Ally's on-balance-sheet funding in March 2026, making digitally acquired customer deposits central to its lending economics.

Inter operates a Brazilian digital banking super-app integrating checking accounts, credit, investments, insurance, and commerce. Its platform exceeded 44 million customers in March 2026, while its newly licensed Miami branch supports direct issuance of U.S. banking products for international customers.

KakaoBank operates a mobile-first Korean banking platform offering deposits, unsecured credit, mortgages, and financial products distributed through its app. Its association with the Kakao digital ecosystem supports customer acquisition and engagement without the extensive physical branch infrastructure of traditional Korean banks.

Rakuten Bank uses online account acquisition and integrations with the Rakuten ecosystem to gather deposits and provide banking services in Japan. Its October 2026 restructuring brought Rakuten Card and Rakuten Securities Holdings under the listed bank, broadening its financial-services offering beyond deposits and payments.

First Internet Bank was the first U.S. state-chartered FDIC-insured institution to operate entirely online. Its branchless model supports digital deposits alongside nationwide SBA, franchise, consumer, and commercial lending, with $4.8 billion in deposits at June 2026.

EQB operates Canada's EQ Bank digital deposit platform alongside Equitable Bank's lending and mortgage businesses. EQ Bank's app-based savings and everyday banking products provide direct-to-consumer funding without a conventional nationwide branch network, complementing its alternative mortgage and commercial lending operations.

LendingClub operates a nationally chartered digital bank combining online personal loan origination with deposit accounts and marketplace loan distribution. Its Happen Bank rebranding in 2026 reflects its expansion beyond peer-to-peer lending toward digitally acquired banking relationships and recurring consumer financial services.

The Bancorp distributes banking services through fintech partners rather than a conventional retail branch network. Its Fintech Solutions division reported more than 50 million active accounts and over 40 fintech partners in July 2026, supporting card issuance, payment processing, and embedded banking.

Chime distributes mobile banking and payment products to more than 10 million active members through partner banks. Its September 2026 agreement to acquire Stride Bank could bring banking infrastructure in-house, although the transaction had not yet closed at announcement.

Pathward operates a partner-driven banking model supporting prepaid cards, consumer lending, tax refund products, and embedded financial services. Its distribution through financial technology companies and tax preparation providers enables nationwide customer reach without a conventional consumer branch network.

Coastal's CCBX platform enables fintech partners to distribute digital deposits, debit and credit cards, and lending products without establishing their own bank. The platform had 22 active partners in June 2026, complementing Coastal's physical community banking franchise in Washington.

home_feed_events.title: Banks '24: Digital & Branch-Light Banks - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Evercore is an independent advisory firm specializing in major mergers, acquisitions, restructurings, and strategic corporate transactions. Its 2026 M&A advisory fee ranking places it among the largest global advisers despite lacking the lending balance sheet and institutional trading operations of universal banks.

Goldman Sachs combines leading global M&A advisory, equity and debt underwriting, prime brokerage, derivatives, and institutional market-making. Its Global Banking & Markets division benefits from corporate transactions and client trading activity, while its FICC franchise intermediates interest-rate, credit, currency, and commodity risks.

Houlihan Lokey specializes in middle-market M&A, financial restructuring, and financial and valuation advisory. Its restructuring franchise advises creditors and distressed companies, giving it an earnings driver that can strengthen during credit-market stress when conventional acquisition activity weakens.

Jefferies operates a global investment banking and capital-markets platform with substantial middle-market and large-cap advisory, leveraged finance, equities, and fixed-income businesses. Its investment banking franchise has expanded its share of equity underwriting and M&A fees, supported by sector-specialist bankers and institutional distribution.

Morgan Stanley combines global investment banking with institutional equities, fixed-income trading, prime brokerage, and capital financing. Its extensive equities franchise includes cash trading, derivatives, and services for hedge funds, while its wealth-management distribution network complements institutional securities issuance.

Lazard's Financial Advisory business provides M&A, restructuring, sovereign advisory, and capital structure advice across international markets. Its asset-management division diversifies revenue, but its distinctive investment-banking exposure comes from cross-border strategic mandates and sovereign restructuring expertise.

PJT operates independent strategic advisory, restructuring, and capital-raising businesses. PJT Partners and PJT Camberview serve corporate boards and investors on strategic transactions and shareholder matters, while its restructuring practice advises companies and creditors on liability management and complex financial reorganizations.

Moelis provides independent M&A, restructuring, recapitalization, and capital-structure advisory services without relying on securities trading or traditional bank lending. Its restructuring and capital solutions practices create opportunities from corporate liability management and private capital transactions alongside conventional mergers.

Piper Sandler focuses on middle-market investment banking, particularly financial institutions, healthcare, industrials, and public finance. Its 2025 advisory revenue reached approximately $1.04 billion, complemented by healthcare equity underwriting and municipal finance businesses serving specialized issuer groups.

Raymond James operates an investment banking franchise serving middle-market companies through M&A advisory, equity underwriting, and debt financing. Its Capital Markets segment combines these services with institutional fixed-income and equities operations, supported by its broader financial adviser and wealth-management network.

Stifel combines middle-market investment banking, institutional brokerage, and securities underwriting. Its Keefe, Bruyette & Woods subsidiary specializes in financial institutions, providing M&A and capital-raising expertise to banks, insurers, and other financial businesses that require industry-specific regulatory and balance-sheet knowledge.

BofA Securities combines global debt and equity capital markets, leveraged finance, and corporate advisory with institutional trading operations. Its particularly strong bond and loan underwriting franchises leverage Bank of America's corporate banking relationships to originate and distribute financing for large issuers.

Citi's Banking and Markets businesses combine corporate advisory, debt and equity underwriting, leveraged finance, and institutional trading. Its extensive multinational corporate relationships support cross-border financing and capital-market transactions, while its Markets franchise provides fixed-income, currencies, equities, and securities financing services.

JPMorgan leads global investment-banking fee rankings through a broad platform covering M&A, equity issuance, debt underwriting, and syndicated lending. Its Markets business adds rates, currencies, credit, equities, and commodities trading, making it a major intermediary in corporate and institutional capital formation.

Barclays Investment Bank combines a major transatlantic fixed-income and equities trading platform with debt underwriting, leveraged finance, and M&A advisory. Its London and New York operations connect European and American issuers with institutional investors, particularly through credit, rates, and structured financing.

Deutsche Bank's Investment Bank includes substantial fixed-income and currency trading, debt origination, financing, and advisory operations. Its position in European credit markets, structured finance, and foreign exchange makes institutional market activity an important driver alongside its German corporate banking franchise.

Perella Weinberg is an independent advisory firm focused on mergers, acquisitions, restructuring, liability management, and capital solutions. Its advisory-only model minimizes reliance on lending or trading balance sheets, concentrating revenue on corporate strategic decisions and complex financial transactions.

UBS Investment Bank provides global advisory, equity capital markets, fixed-income financing, derivatives, and institutional securities services. Its integration of Credit Suisse expanded and reshaped institutional capabilities, while its large wealth-management distribution network provides access to private investors and corporate decision-makers.

CITIC Securities is a major Chinese securities firm providing domestic equity and bond underwriting, institutional brokerage, derivatives, and M&A advisory. Its franchise links Chinese corporations and institutional investors with mainland capital markets and Hong Kong international financing channels.

BNP Paribas Corporate and Institutional Banking combines global markets, securities financing, corporate advisory, and debt and equity underwriting. Its European issuer relationships and fixed-income franchise provide substantial exposure to euro-denominated bond markets and financing for multinational corporations.

RBC Capital Markets provides investment banking, debt and equity underwriting, institutional trading, and corporate financing across North America and international markets. Its established Canadian franchise supports resource-sector financing, corporate debt issuance, and cross-border transactions involving Canadian issuers.

StoneX intermediates global commodity, currency, equity, and fixed-income markets for commercial clients and institutions. Its physical commodities, hedging, clearing, and execution businesses distinguish its capital-markets exposure from traditional M&A advisers and corporate underwriting franchises.

CICC specializes in Chinese corporate financing, investment banking, institutional securities, and cross-border capital markets. Its historical position advising major Chinese enterprises and arranging international share offerings provides distinctive exposure to Chinese privatizations, Hong Kong listings, and outbound transactions.

home_feed_events.title: Banks '24: Investment Banking & Capital Markets - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Esquire Bank specializes in lending and deposit services for litigation law firms, including financing supported by legal case portfolios. Its second-quarter 2026 presentation reported approximately 8.8% yields on law firm loans, complemented by a nationwide merchant payment-processing franchise.

Live Oak operates a nationwide small-business lending platform specializing in SBA 7(a) and USDA-guaranteed credit. Its industry-specific teams originate loans to selected professional and commercial verticals, while Government Loan Solutions provides settlement, accounting, and securitization services for guaranteed loan programs.

Triumph focuses on transportation finance through freight invoice factoring, payments, and freight transaction intelligence. Its Triumph Network connects carriers, freight brokers, and other transportation participants, while TBK Bank provides banking infrastructure supporting a specialized ecosystem of freight-related financial transactions.

The Bancorp uses deposits generated through fintech sponsorship to fund specialized lending, including securities-backed credit, multifamily bridge loans, SBA finance, and fleet leasing. At June 2026, 96% of deposits came from Fintech Solutions, demonstrating its unusual partner-driven funding structure.

Coastal's CCBX division provides embedded lending, card issuance, and deposit sponsorship for fintech partners alongside its Washington community bank. Its June 2026 results included a $68.8 million credit expense linked to one partner relationship, highlighting the distinctive underwriting and counterparty risks of sponsor banking.

FinWise originates consumer and business credit through fintech Strategic Program partners, combining bank underwriting oversight with externally sourced borrowers. Strategic Program loans held for investment totaled $144.6 million in June 2026, representing 25.3% of its loan portfolio, alongside SBA lending and commercial leasing.

Pathward combines commercial specialty finance with tax-season financial products and partner-originated consumer lending. Its Refund Advance program originated approximately $1.87 billion during the 2026 tax season, generating product revenue through relationships with tax preparation providers and creating a highly seasonal lending niche.

VersaBank purchases structured receivables from financing partners, providing funding for point-of-sale consumer and small-business loans rather than originating conventional branch loans. Its Real-Time Structured Receivable Program began operating in 2026, allowing partners to finance individual receivables without lengthy warehouse funding periods.

Axos combines nationwide digital deposit gathering with specialized institutional and commercial lending, including lender finance, fund finance, securities-backed credit, and commercial real estate. Its fiduciary deposit platform serves bankruptcy trustees and court-appointed receivers, creating a differentiated funding source.

Customers operates specialized lending teams covering venture-backed companies, commercial equipment finance, mortgage warehouse lending, and private investment funds. Its fund finance business provides capital-call facilities secured by limited-partner commitments and financing backed by portfolios of private credit assets.

First Internet Bank uses its branchless deposit model to fund nationwide specialty lending, including SBA loans, franchise finance, single-tenant lease financing, and public finance. At June 2026, its small-business lending portfolio held $436 million in retained balances and a larger serviced SBA portfolio.

ServisFirst operates a specialized correspondent banking business serving more than 380 financial institutions across 31 states and Washington, D.C. Its offerings include liquidity services, correspondent relationships, and an agent credit-card program for community banks alongside its conventional commercial banking franchise.

home_feed_events.title: Banks '24: Specialty Banking & Niche Lending - new theme

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Citi's Treasury and Trade Solutions business provides multinational companies with payments, collections, liquidity management, trade finance, and commercial cards across its extensive international banking network. Its ability to maintain banking relationships in numerous local markets is especially valuable to corporations operating across currencies and jurisdictions.

J.P. Morgan Payments combines corporate treasury services, merchant acquiring, liquidity management, and international money movement. Its network supports complex multinational cash-management structures, while blockchain-based payment infrastructure and API connectivity increasingly integrate the bank directly into corporate treasury operations.

Bank of America's Global Payments Solutions business serves corporate and institutional clients through CashPro, providing payment initiation, receivables management, cash forecasting, and liquidity services. CashPro's integration with corporate finance workflows distinguishes its treasury franchise from banks focused primarily on conventional commercial lending.

HSBC's Global Payments Solutions and Global Trade Solutions operations connect corporate clients across Asia, Europe, and the Middle East. Its extensive international network supports multicurrency liquidity structures, cross-border receivables, documentary trade finance, and companies managing supply chains across Asian and Western markets.

Standard Chartered's Transaction Services franchise includes Cash Management and Trade & Working Capital operations. Its strength lies in connecting multinational companies across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East, especially emerging-market corridors where local banking access and foreign-exchange capabilities are important.

Deutsche Bank's Corporate Bank provides cash management, trade finance, securities-related services, and institutional payments. Its German corporate relationships and international branch network support multinational treasury operations, while its euro clearing and correspondent banking capabilities provide financial infrastructure beyond traditional corporate lending.

BNP Paribas provides corporate cash management, international payments, trade finance, and liquidity services through its Transaction Banking operations. Its substantial continental European corporate banking franchise gives it a strong position in euro-denominated cash management and cross-border treasury services for multinational businesses.

Barclays provides corporate payments, collections, liquidity management, and trade finance through its UK Corporate Bank and international operations. Its sterling clearing capabilities and established relationships with British companies give it distinctive exposure to UK corporate treasury activity and international businesses operating in sterling.

Société Générale offers cash management, international trade finance, and correspondent banking to corporate and financial institution clients. Its Global Transaction Banking activities connect French and European corporate relationships with international markets, including specialized trade and structured commodity finance capabilities.

Wells Fargo's Global Treasury Management business provides receivables processing, commercial payments, liquidity services, and corporate cash management. Its extensive U.S. commercial banking relationships create opportunities to capture operating deposits and payment flows from middle-market and larger corporate customers.

MUFG provides global transaction banking through cash management, trade finance, foreign exchange, and corporate liquidity services. Its Japanese corporate relationships create cross-border treasury opportunities as major Japanese manufacturers and trading houses manage international subsidiaries, suppliers, and multicurrency working capital.

U.S. Bank combines corporate treasury management with Elavon merchant acquiring, commercial card programs, and payment technology. Its receivables, payables, and integrated payments services connect business operating accounts with payment processing infrastructure, giving it a differentiated domestic transaction banking franchise.

ING's Wholesale Banking operations provide payments, cash management, working capital solutions, and trade finance to multinational corporations. Its European banking network and financial technology integrations help corporate clients centralize liquidity, automate treasury workflows, and manage international commercial payments.

PNC's Treasury Management business provides corporate payments, receivables processing, liquidity solutions, and integrated payable services through PINACLE. Its commercial banking relationships and treasury technology help businesses manage operating cash, working capital, and financial workflows across multiple U.S. markets.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: Japanese prestige beauty company owning SHISEIDO, Clé de Peau Beauté, ANESSA, and ELIXIR. Its advanced skincare research, sun-protection formulations, and premium department-store distribution underpin its J-Beauty exposure, while NARS and Drunk Elephant extend its international cosmetics and skincare reach.

Operates DECORTÉ, SEKKISEI, ADDICTION, Visee, and FASIO across prestige skincare, sunscreen, and color cosmetics. Its proprietary skincare research and portfolio spanning department stores and drugstores give it significant exposure to Japanese formulation innovation and domestic and international beauty consumption.

Operates Japanese beauty brands including Kanebo, Curél, SENSAI, Bioré, and LUNASOL. Its skin-barrier research, facial cleansing products, and cosmetics formulation capabilities are complemented by professional haircare operations, although household products and chemicals dilute consolidated beauty exposure.

Owns Hada Labo, Melano CC, Skin Aqua, and Obagi-branded skincare operations in Japan. Its pharmaceutical research background supports hyaluronic-acid moisturizers, vitamin C formulations, and sunscreen products sold primarily through accessible retail channels, distinguishing its dermatological approach to beauty.

Owns POLA, ORBIS, THREE, and Jurlique, spanning premium anti-aging skincare, direct-to-consumer cosmetics, and botanical beauty products. POLA's beauty consultation network and ORBIS's direct distribution create distinctive customer relationships, supported by Japanese skincare research and proprietary formulations.

Develops ReFa beauty devices, hair dryers, styling irons, showerheads, and related haircare and skincare products. Its ReFa ecosystem connects premium home beauty equipment with salons and consumer retail, while its separate SIXPAD wellness business reduces overall beauty concentration.

Specializes in home beauty technology including Photo PLUS facial devices, RF treatments, EMS devices, and skincare designed for use alongside its equipment. Its proprietary beauty hardware and companion consumables distinguish it from conventional cosmetics brands and professional clinic equipment manufacturers.

Operates BOTANIST botanical haircare and YOLU nighttime haircare, emphasizing distinctive product concepts, packaging, and digital merchandising. Its concentrated shampoo and treatment portfolio captures Japanese drugstore beauty spending and demand for differentiated, premium-positioned everyday haircare.

Develops professional salon haircare, hair color, and treatment products, including the Aujua and global milbon franchises. Its salon education programs, stylist relationships, and specialized haircare formulations create a professional distribution ecosystem rather than relying primarily on mass-market retail.

Produces professional haircare products including COTA i CARE and COTA COUTURE shampoos and treatments. Its salon-exclusive distribution and consultation-based product selection support recurring purchases through stylists, creating concentrated exposure to Japanese professional haircare rather than general cosmetics retail.

Owns Noevir prestige skincare, NOV dermatological cosmetics, and other beauty brands. NOV develops products for sensitive and acne-prone skin, while Noevir uses beauty consultation and direct distribution, differentiating its skincare business from conventional drugstore-oriented manufacturers.

Operates PERFECT ONE, known for all-in-one skincare gels designed to simplify daily routines. Its direct marketing, recurring customer relationships, and focus on mature skincare consumers provide differentiated exposure to Japanese anti-aging beauty and convenient multifunctional formulations.

Japanese prestige skincare company operating AXXZIA and AGTHEORY, including eye-care and anti-aging skincare products. Its international distribution, particularly connections to Chinese consumers, and premium retail presence distinguish its export-oriented model from predominantly domestic Japanese beauty brands.

Operates an internet-focused direct-to-consumer business selling proprietary health and beauty products, including HYALO DEEP PATCH skincare. Its in-house digital advertising, customer service, e-commerce operations, and subscription model create an alternative Japanese beauty distribution model focused on repeat purchases.

Supplies beauty accessories, cosmetic tools, and related products including makeup implements and decorative contact lenses. Its exposure comes from accessories used alongside cosmetics rather than selling major skincare formulations, adding a specialized beauty merchandising and product-design business.

Manufactures and sells wigs, hairpieces, and hair-restoration products, supported by specialized consultation and fitting services. Its physical retail and service network monetizes appearance-focused hair replacement, making it a distinctive Japanese beauty-adjacent business outside traditional cosmetics and skincare.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: BNP Paribas operates major commercial and retail banking franchises in France, Belgium, Italy, and Luxembourg alongside European corporate and institutional banking. Its integrated eurozone network provides corporate cash management, financing, securities services, and consumer credit across several important continental banking markets.

HSBC connects European corporate and wealth clients with Asian and Middle Eastern markets through international banking, trade finance, and global payments. Its London headquarters and substantial UK banking franchise coexist with an unusually Asia-oriented earnings mix, distinguishing it from domestically focused European lenders.

Intesa Sanpaolo combines extensive Italian retail and commercial banking with insurance, wealth management, and asset management through Eurizon. Its large Italian household and SME customer base generates deposits and lending relationships, while fee-based financial products diversify revenues beyond net interest income.

UniCredit operates major commercial banking businesses in Italy, Germany, Austria, and Central and Eastern Europe. Its cross-border franchise benefits from European corporate lending and deposit relationships, while its expanding Commerzbank shareholding creates a distinctive potential consolidation catalyst subject to remaining transaction conditions.

Crédit Agricole SA provides listed exposure to the broader Crédit Agricole banking group's French and international financial-services operations, including LCL, corporate banking, insurance, and Amundi. Its cooperative group relationships and diversified fee-generating businesses distinguish it from straightforward listed retail banking franchises.

Barclays combines UK personal banking, credit cards, and corporate banking with a large transatlantic investment bank. Its Barclays UK franchise provides domestic mortgage and deposit exposure, while the investment bank connects European borrowers and securities markets with institutional investors in the United States.

BBVA operates a large Spanish banking franchise alongside substantial Mexican, Turkish, and South American operations. Its Spanish corporate and retail banking network provides exposure to eurozone credit conditions, while its extensive mobile-banking capabilities differentiate its customer acquisition and operating model.

ING operates digital retail and commercial banking franchises across several European countries, complemented by international wholesale banking. Its large Dutch, Belgian, and German customer bases provide deposits and lending demand, while its digital distribution model reduces dependence on extensive physical branch networks.

Santander combines major banking franchises in Spain, the UK, Portugal, and Poland with substantial Latin American operations. Its European businesses provide consumer deposits, mortgages, vehicle finance, and commercial banking, while international diversification makes its earnings less exclusively dependent on eurozone conditions.

UBS combines Swiss domestic banking with one of the world's largest wealth-management platforms and an international investment bank. Its integration of Credit Suisse creates a distinctive Swiss banking concentration and significant restructuring responsibilities, while wealth management makes its earnings less dependent on conventional European lending.

Deutsche Bank combines German corporate and private banking with international investment banking, fixed-income trading, and transaction services. Its relationships with major German exporters and industrial companies create direct exposure to European manufacturing, international trade, and corporate financing conditions.

Société Générale combines French retail banking through SG with international banking, global markets, and vehicle leasing through Ayvens. Its equity derivatives franchise and financing operations provide capital-markets exposure, while French household and commercial banking remain important domestic earnings drivers.

Lloyds is heavily exposed to domestic British banking through Lloyds Bank, Halifax, and Bank of Scotland. Its mortgage lending, current accounts, SME banking, and consumer credit businesses provide relatively concentrated exposure to UK household finances, property transactions, and sterling deposit margins.

NatWest operates a predominantly UK-focused banking franchise serving households, SMEs, commercial businesses, and affluent customers. Its NatWest, Royal Bank of Scotland, and Coutts brands connect domestic deposit gathering with business lending, mortgage financing, and private banking services.

Standard Chartered is headquartered in London but earns much of its banking revenue from Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. Its corporate transaction services and emerging-market wealth businesses connect European institutions with international trade and financing corridors rather than providing primarily domestic European credit exposure.

CaixaBank has a particularly extensive Spanish retail banking network following its combination with Bankia. Its large household deposit base, mortgage portfolio, consumer relationships, and insurance distribution make Spanish interest rates, housing demand, and domestic banking competition central to earnings.

Commerzbank concentrates on German SMEs, corporate customers, and retail clients through its Mittelstandsbank and domestic banking operations. Its mBank subsidiary provides Polish exposure, while UniCredit's proposed control transaction creates a separate potential restructuring and ownership catalyst.

Danske Bank combines leading Danish personal and business banking operations with important Norwegian, Swedish, and Finnish customer relationships. Its Danish mortgage and corporate banking activities connect the group's earnings to Nordic housing finance, business investment, and domestic deposit competition.

Erste operates a major Austrian banking franchise alongside significant retail and commercial banks in Central and Eastern Europe. Its exposure to Czech, Slovak, Romanian, Hungarian, and other regional customers links earnings to household credit penetration, local deposits, and regional economic convergence.

KBC combines Belgian banking and insurance with substantial operations in the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, and Bulgaria. Its integrated bancassurance model generates lending, deposit, and insurance income, while Central European expansion distinguishes its earnings exposure from banks focused solely on Western Europe.

Nordea operates large retail, corporate, and wealth-management businesses across Finland, Sweden, Denmark, and Norway. Its cross-Nordic franchise combines residential mortgages, household deposits, asset management, and corporate banking across economies with distinct currencies, housing markets, and monetary conditions.

Banco BPM is a major Italian retail and commercial bank with strong roots in Lombardy and other Northern Italian business markets. Its relationships with SMEs, households, and local enterprises create concentrated exposure to Italian corporate borrowing, mortgage activity, and domestic banking consolidation.

DNB is Norway's largest banking group, financing households, businesses, commercial real estate, shipping, and energy-related industries. Its Norwegian deposit and mortgage franchises coexist with specialized offshore, maritime, and energy lending, giving it unusually direct exposure to Norway's resource-linked corporate economy.

PKO Bank Polski operates one of Poland's largest domestic banking franchises, serving households, SMEs, and corporations through extensive branches and digital services. Its Polish zloty deposits, mortgages, and commercial lending provide direct exposure to domestic consumption, wage growth, and business investment.

SEB emphasizes large corporate and institutional banking across Sweden and Northern Europe, alongside Baltic retail and commercial operations. Its relationships with Nordic industrial groups support cash management, financing, foreign exchange, and capital-markets services, differentiating it from predominantly household-mortgage-focused lenders.

holdings_preview.ticker_note: MUFG combines Japan's largest banking franchise with international corporate lending, securities services, and trust banking. Its extensive domestic deposit base provides exposure to rising yen interest rates, while its Morgan Stanley relationship and overseas lending operations diversify earnings beyond Japan's credit cycle.

SMFG combines SMBC's domestic retail and corporate banking with international wholesale finance, project lending, and securities operations. Its relationships with major Japanese corporations and midmarket businesses provide exposure to higher domestic loan yields and financing demand, complemented by global corporate banking.

Mizuho combines a major Japanese commercial banking network with Mizuho Securities and institutional capital-markets services. Its relationships with large Japanese manufacturers, corporate bond issuers, and institutional clients link domestic lending and deposits with securities underwriting, syndicated finance, and international capital markets.

Japan Post Bank gathers deposits through Japan's extensive postal network, giving it access to households across urban and rural communities. Its large securities investment portfolio and distinctive nationwide distribution structure make interest-rate changes particularly consequential for asset reinvestment and deposit funding economics.

Resona concentrates on Japanese retail and small-business banking through Resona Bank, Saitama Resona Bank, and other group operations. Its comparatively domestic earnings base, extensive SME relationships, and trust-related financial services create substantial exposure to Japanese deposit pricing and commercial lending conditions.

Shizuoka Financial Group operates Shizuoka Bank, serving manufacturers, exporters, households, and local businesses in an industrial prefecture between Tokyo and Nagoya. Its relationships with automotive and machinery suppliers create exposure to Japanese industrial investment, while regional deposits support its lending franchise.

Yokohama Financial Group operates the Bank of Yokohama and Higashi-Nippon Bank, concentrating on customers around Kanagawa and the greater Tokyo economy. Its dense metropolitan deposit franchise and SME relationships provide exposure to commercial borrowing, household finances, and lending competition in Japan's largest economic region.

Sumitomo Mitsui Trust combines Japanese trust banking, institutional custody, pension administration, investment management, and real estate-related services. Its substantial fiduciary and asset-servicing businesses distinguish its fee income from ordinary commercial banks, while its balance sheet remains exposed to Japanese funding conditions.

Chiba Bank serves households, property owners, and businesses across Chiba Prefecture and the greater Tokyo metropolitan area. Its residential mortgage and commercial lending franchises connect the bank to suburban population patterns, regional property markets, and business activity around Narita Airport and Tokyo.

Fukuoka Financial Group operates Bank of Fukuoka, Kumamoto Bank, and other regional banking businesses across Kyushu. Its exposure to northern Kyushu's manufacturing, logistics, and semiconductor investment activity, including the Kumamoto chipmaking ecosystem, differentiates its regional commercial lending opportunity.

Rakuten Bank gathers deposits and distributes banking products digitally through online accounts and integrations with the Rakuten ecosystem. Its retail payments, deposits, consumer lending, and financial-platform relationships provide a branch-light alternative to Japan's conventional regional banking networks.

Kyoto Financial Group operates the Bank of Kyoto, which maintains longstanding relationships with Kyoto-area manufacturers, technology companies, and local businesses. Its portfolio of strategic corporate shareholdings distinguishes its capital management and securities exposure from typical Japanese regional lenders.

Mebuki combines Joyo Bank and Ashikaga Bank, providing extensive banking coverage across Ibaraki, Tochigi, and neighboring areas north of Tokyo. Its lending to manufacturers, agricultural businesses, and local households reflects a diversified regional economy with links to metropolitan supply chains.

Chugin operates Chugoku Bank, focusing on Okayama and neighboring western Japanese prefectures. Its commercial relationships with machinery manufacturers, materials producers, transportation businesses, and local SMEs provide lending exposure to the industrial and logistics economy surrounding the Seto Inland Sea.

Kyushu Financial Group operates Higo Bank and Kagoshima Bank, serving businesses and households across southern Kyushu. Its regional lending relationships connect the franchise to agriculture, tourism, local manufacturing, and the expansion of semiconductor-related industrial activity in Kumamoto.

Daishi Hokuetsu operates a consolidated regional banking franchise centered on Niigata Prefecture. Its business lending, household deposits, and agricultural relationships connect earnings to local manufacturers, food processors, rice-producing communities, and a regional economy facing long-term demographic challenges.

Hirogin operates Hiroshima Bank, a major commercial lender in western Japan. Its relationships with automotive suppliers, machinery manufacturers, transportation companies, and local SMEs connect regional credit demand to Hiroshima's industrial economy and the broader manufacturing supply chains of the Chugoku region.

SBI Shinsei combines retail deposits, structured finance, corporate lending, and consumer financial services with SBI Group distribution relationships. Its specialty financing operations and links to SBI's wider digital financial ecosystem differentiate its business from conventional Japanese deposit-funded regional banks.

Aozora operates a distinctive Japanese banking model combining retail deposits with structured finance, corporate lending, and investment activities. Its exposure to domestic and overseas commercial real estate and specialized financing makes securities valuation and credit underwriting particularly important alongside Japanese funding conditions.

Hokuhoku operates Hokuriku Bank and Hokkaido Bank, spanning two geographically distinct Japanese regional economies. Its banking relationships include Hokuriku manufacturers and Hokkaido agricultural, tourism, and service businesses, creating exposure to varied local credit markets and regional financing demand.

Iyogin operates Iyo Bank, serving Shikoku and surrounding business markets. Its lending relationships with regional manufacturers, shipping companies, maritime operators, and local households provide a differentiated connection to western Japan's shipbuilding and maritime-industrial economy.

Seven Bank operates banking and cash-access infrastructure centered on ATMs located in Seven-Eleven stores and other retail sites. Its transaction-driven fee model, digital banking services, and ATM network distinguish its earnings from regional banks reliant primarily on interest spreads from conventional lending.

Okinawa Financial Group operates Bank of Okinawa, serving households and businesses across the island prefecture. Its regional deposit and lending relationships provide direct exposure to tourism, hospitality, construction, residential property, and the distinctive economic conditions of Japan's southern island economy.

Juroku operates Juroku Bank in Gifu and surrounding central Japanese markets, serving households, small businesses, and industrial manufacturers. Its commercial relationships span manufacturing suppliers, regional exporters, and businesses linked to the automotive and machinery industries of central Honshu.
